## MAP-INTEGRATE-2 R — OQ-556 original-code verdict — 2026-11-12 — APPROVED

OQ-556 is settled: the state-138 forward home search matches the original. This package changes
documentation only; it changes no behavior, rule default, serialization, stream, fixture or state
identity.

Read-only disassembly of GOG `AnnoWelt.dll`, SHA-256
`f220a878510f740c4cfb7224ade0a260e9a0fd7e99113e1201e7a37c0dfa6ae2`, established the complete
original path:

- The start flood is `0x10003aa0`-`0x10003d81`. Each call seeds one selected, quantized sub-cell
  at `0x10003b68`-`0x10003b98`, expands cardinally at `0x10003ba2`-`0x10003cb6`, and writes edge
  keys at `0x10003cbc`-`0x10003d75`. The four admission masks are `0x2111@0x10006a81`,
  `0x8444@0x10006c69`, `0x4888@0x10006dd0` and `0x1222@0x10006e8c`.
- Goal setup is `0x10003f91`-`0x1000415f`, including the mark at
  `0x10004065`-`0x10004070` and the key-helper call/store at
  `0x10004137`-`0x1000414b`. The search pop loop `0x10004749`-`0x10004794` calls goal-test
  `0x10003220`; dispatcher loop `0x10003708`-`0x1000373d` invokes the installed callback through
  its indirect call at `0x10003737`.
- Home entrances and the callback are installed at `0x10057ae0`-`0x10057bbe`; the installed
  first-goal-stop callback is `0x10054240`. A no-path result takes the original failure branches
  at `0x10053d20` and `0x10053f50`.

Ghidra was **NOT_RUN** because neither Ghidra nor a Java runtime is installed on this Mac. The
repository's `tools/disasm.py` fallback was used against the identified DLL, and the independent
reviewer separately re-read the resulting instructions and address ranges.

### Focused original-data proof

The author probe loaded real `endless02` island 12, object 3110 at tile (322,770), walk code 4 and
mask `0x139`. Classified counts: selected 1 / executed 1 / failed 0 / empty 0 / skipped 0;
assertions 16/16. It reproduces all nine start keys and proves that starts `(0,1)`, `(0,2)` and
`(1,2)` reach no goal for all three affected homes, while all other six starts reach a goal.
`oq556-probe-final.log`, SHA-256
`fa43d8c60366f1554586a71b904a238ea24a0bf6c655ba370405ae0b699ff17b`.

Independent reviewer `/root/integrate2_r_review` approved the final two-file docs diff with no

/ failed 0 / empty 0 / skipped 0; assertions 16/16. `reviewer-final-probe.log`, SHA-256
`e754c576f92dbfe66050a06aead9ea5b5ff2729d0fa12a5df2a90fab279aafcc`. Its probe binary SHA-256

### Decisions and reasoning

Base `origin/orch/land-gate-1b` db118177, branch `task/GATE-1c`, code head `3b311a8e`, pushed head

**Item 1, the flow-build test (`river_flow_corpus_test.cpp:1322`).** Cause, with evidence: its
"nothing is rebuilt any more" check summed `update_chunks`'s global `built` return, which also
counts its margin/neighbouring-group housekeeping chunks (`margin_keys()`/`adjacent_keys()`,
`frame.cpp` `request_chunks`/`plan_margin`); those are not required to have finished their own
in-flight build by the time the loop above finds every *visible* chunk settled (that loop only
polls `visible_chunks(view)`), so one can still arrive inside the 60-iteration/300 ms check window.
Reproduced at Debug (`/Od`, no Ninja preset on this host, so MSVC Debug stood in for `-O0`) with
temporary logging: 3/40 runs failed with `CHECK(rebuilt == 0)` violated by exactly one chunk; one
capture showed an **adjacent** key (`g=0,-3,8`) still uncached (`cached=0`) at the moment the
settled-loop declared every visible chunk settled, then arriving on the very first follow-up
iteration (`built=1`). Fix: track this test's own view's cached-chunk pointer identity across the
60-iteration window instead of the global count (no sleep/frame/retry count changed). Proof: 80/80
Debug reruns clean after the fix (40 fresh + 40 at the same condition that showed the three
original failures); a deliberately-broken variant (temporarily forcing one recorded pointer to
`nullptr,` simulating a real rebuild) fails with `CHECK( ...chunk(...) == before_rebuild[...] )` at

## COORD-FLAKE-1 — the two test-coordinator flakes, cause first — 2026-11-13 — READY FOR REVIEW

Base `origin/task/GATE-1c` `9a958dc1` (GATE-1c not yet on `main`, so no merge needed), branch
`task/COORD-FLAKE-1`, head `a7dedc90`.

**F3 (D1, deaf), `cpp (macos-clang)`.** Evidence: runs `43123068877` (test #76, `SIGPIPE***Exception`,
2.23s) and `43082536481` (`INCOMPLETE`, same test, no assertion failed, no doctest output at all
between `Start` and the signal) — 2 occurrences since 2026-11-10, matching the packet's citation; no
further occurrences found in the other failed runs checked in that window (`42883218166` is an
unrelated `V3` failure). Mechanism, read from the code: `budget_probe.cpp`'s `deaf_listener` already
calls `startup_sockets()` (landed 2026-11-10, `ee504b75`) to ignore `SIGPIPE` for *its own* socket
sends. That fix never touched the *parent* test process. `budget_f3_test.cpp`'s D1-deaf case spawns
the client as `probe({"reqwait", ...})`; `reqwait` mode (`budget_probe.cpp:474-503`) exits right after
printing `RESULT` when the reservation is refused — only the *admitted* branch waits for `quit`. The
parent's `quit_and_wait(deaf)` → `client.send("q\n")` (`budget_f3_test.cpp:550`) then races a
`::write()` to that already-closed stdin pipe; the parent process never set `SIGPIPE` to ignore
(nothing in `main.cpp` or this path does), so the default disposition (terminate) kills the whole
ctest process — not a timeout, not a crash in the child, a broken-pipe write in the parent. Not
reproduced directly as a SIGPIPE locally (POSIX-only, and this host's CPU load didn't widen the race
enough), but the mechanism is read from the source, not guessed: the exact asymmetry (`reqwait`
waits for quit only when admitted) is a verifiable, named line, and `Child::send()`'s missing
liveness check applies to all 10 `.send("q...")` call sites in the suite, any of which could race the
same way. Fix: `Child::send()` (`child_process.hpp`) now skips the write when `running()` says the
child has already exited, and ignores `SIGPIPE` as a backstop for the remaining gap between that
check and the write — the same pattern `coord_wire.hpp`'s socket paths already use. Proof: WSL `-O1`
ASan, `*deaf*bounded deadline*`, 60/60 clean (no regression from the fix); MSVC Release, same case,
passes (Windows has no `SIGPIPE`, so this proves no regression, not the crash itself, which is
POSIX-only).

**C3, `cpp (windows-msvc)`.** Evidence: run `43218940794` attempt 1, test `#71`,
`REQUIRE( has(holder.line(10000ms), "READY 1") )` false, 0.35s total — the FIRST assertion of the
test, failing fast, not timing out. 1 occurrence found since 2026-11-10 (the packet's own citation);
no others found in the runs checked. Read `budget.cpp`, `coord.cpp`, `coord_server.cpp`,
`budget_f2_test.cpp`'s `Scope`/`start_coord`/port assignment (`port_for`, globally unique per file and
index — ruled out a port collision) and `admit_deadline()` (default 1800s, ruling out a slow
coordinator-connect retry as the 0.35s cause: that path would hang for minutes, not fail in
under a second). Could not reproduce: 30 isolated runs under 8 background CPU-spin jobs, and 6 full
`ctest -j 16 --repeat until-fail:1` passes of the whole `anno_test_support_tests` suite under the
same load (one unrelated `F4 (N4)` failure turned up from a stale WSL-coordinator-binary path,
unrelated to C3), all clean; 0/36 total. No line in the evidence or the code read points to a single,
provable mechanism the way F3's does — only candidates I could not confirm (a readiness check that
accepts a silent-but-running coordinator, which the "pre-F2 binary" comment suggests is for an old
coordinator build, not this scenario; a possible fast `Decision::Refuse` with no visible cause).
Per the packet, not fixed: the evidence does not prove a cause, and a guess-fix here would not close
this by its mechanism, only by chance. Not reproduced, no fix applied, raising a QUESTION instead.

Gates: `ctest -R anno_test_support_tests` (canonical runner), MSVC Release: `selected=79 executed=76
failed=0 skipped=3 (platform=3) sanitizer_lines=0 PASS`. WSL `-O1` ASan, same selection:
`selected=93 executed=89 failed=0 skipped=4 (opt-in=4) sanitizer_lines=0 PASS`. Hosted CI: pending on
this push (read after push, per the rule).

NOT_RUN: the full WSL gate and the MSVC game-file run (the orchestrator, at the merge); TEST-MEM-1;
C3's fix (unproven cause).

Decisions and reasoning:
- Fixed F3 at the one shared call site (`Child::send()`) rather than only `budget_f3_test.cpp`'s own
  `quit_and_wait`: all 10 `.send("q...")` sites share the same latent race, and the fix needs no
  caller to remember to check first.
- Did not change `reqwait`'s own early-return-on-refusal behavior: exiting promptly once its own
  work is done is correct; the bug is the *caller* not checking liveness before writing, not the
  child exiting when it has nothing left to do.
- Left C3 unfixed rather than apply a speculative change (e.g. widening `start_coord`'s readiness
  window) that the evidence does not support: a flake closed by an unproven guess is not closed by
  its mechanism either.
QUESTIONs: C3 could not be reproduced or diagnosed to a provable mechanism in the time available.
Should it stay on `rerun-and-document` (the project's existing precedent for this family) until it
recurs with richer evidence (e.g. instrumented logging added ahead of time), or is there a next step
I'm missing? Otherwise none; independent review is the orchestrator's.

`send("q\n")`, then asserts the case is still running. In the WSL `-O1` ASan build, with the two new
lines of `send()` reverted: the whole ctest process dies, `rc=141` (`SIGPIPE`), zero output — the
same signature as `INCOMPLETE` test #76. Rebuilt with the fix restored: 0/20 fails. Added the
`SIG_IGN`-is-process-wide-and-inherited sentence to `send()`'s comment.

**F3.** Corrected the `ee504b75` comment in `budget_probe.cpp`'s `deaf_listener`: it blamed run
`42820583088`'s SIGPIPE on this listener; ctest reports the signal of the process it started, not of
a child that process spawned. Three occurrences now on record: `42820583088` (before `ee504b75`,
misattributed at the time), `43082536481` and `43123068877` (after it, both the real parent-`send()`
mechanism this packet fixed). `startup_sockets()` stays, as hardening for this listener's own writes
to a peer that can disappear.

**C3.** No guess-fix. Added the kept-line-plus-`INFO` pattern to all 8
`REQUIRE(has(<child>.line(...), ...))` sites in `budget_f2_test.cpp` (the three `Scope`-based tests
the reviewer's reading covered: `C2` loss, `C2` mute, `C3` replace); no behaviour change. Stays open;
reopens with that output the next time it recurs.

Gates, re-run after this round: `ctest -R anno_test_support_tests`, MSVC Release:
`selected=80 executed=77 failed=0 skipped=3 (platform=3) sanitizer_lines=0 PASS` (one more selected:
F2's new regression case). WSL `-O1` ASan, same selection:
`selected=94 executed=90 failed=0 skipped=4 (opt-in=4) sanitizer_lines=0 PASS`. Hosted CI: pending on
this push (read after push, per the rule).

Decisions and reasoning:
- Fixed F1 by raising the liveness margin, not the admission bound or the deadline-plus-cancel
  logic: the margin is what a scheduling stall can outrun, and `budget_f2_test.cpp` already
  established 1000 ms as adequate for the same kind of coordinator stand-in on this project's hosted
  runners.
- Put F2's regression case next to F3 (D1, deaf) in `budget_f3_test.cpp` rather than in a new file:
  it is this exact mechanism, deterministic and POSIX-only, and belongs beside the case it explains.
- Left `reqwait`'s own early-return-on-refusal behaviour alone again (F1 does not touch it): the
  fix is the liveness margin, not the client's choice to exit once its own work is done.
QUESTIONs: none new; the round-1 QUESTION on C3 stands as before.

### Follow-up — a racy CHECK in F2's own regression case — 2026-11-13

Head `a0997aba`'s push hit `cpp (linux-gcc)`/`cpp (linux-gcc-release)`/`gate` red (run `43351375688`):
F2's new case, `CHECK_FALSE(child.running())` right after `wait_eof()`, with `running()` reporting
true. `wait_eof()` only observes the last writer closing its own fd; `running()`'s
`waitpid(WNOHANG)` can still briefly say the child is alive a moment later - either state proves
the same claim (`send()` does not crash this process, via its `running()` early return or its
`SIGPIPE`-ignore backstop), so the assertion tested an implementation timing detail the API never
promised. Dropped it at head `38fc4abc`, documented why. Proof: 0/30 on Windows, 0/20 in WSL `-O1`
ASan; the canonical selection clean on both again (MSVC Release `80/77/0`, WSL `94/90/0`). Hosted CI
pending on this head.

Closing commit (review round 2, comments only, no behaviour change): head `6b096261`, hosted CI
green (run `43363743842`), `gate` included.

Base `task/PLAY-LIVE-1a` `9e920c18`, branch `task/SHIP-ORDER-1`, worktree `anno1503-SHIP-ORDER-1`. No code change:
could not reproduce.

**Reproduction matrix** (`tools/test/viewer_wiring.py` against `opening_controls.script` or a copy, real GPU window
where noted, `anno1503.exe` built from `9e920c18`, game files, manifest `lan5-ship-a.json`, seat 0), varying one
factor from the contract's own launch (`--ship-start ... --seat 0 --speed 200`, CPU, 1280×720):

| Variation | Renderer | Size | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| contract's own launch (baseline) | CPU | 1280×720 | PASS — order accepted, ship arrives |
| + `--rules living` | CPU | 1280×720 | PASS |
| + `--rules living` | CPU | 1024×768 | PASS |
| + `--rules living` | GPU (RTX 4090, Vulkan) | 1024×768 | PASS — stderr confirms `window: drawable 1024x768 px ... density 1.00`, matching the owner's own log line exactly |
| + `--rules living`, then `resize 2560 1369` mid-session, order again | GPU | 1024×768→2560×1369 | PASS, both orders |
| no `--rules` (main `961a9d4a` cannot take the flag at all) | GPU | 1024×768 | PASS |
| + `--rules living --water original` | GPU | 1024×768 | PASS |

Every run: window exit 0, every script step recorded, the sim's own facts (`latest_kind == move`, `latest ==
arrived`, `ship.1.x/y`) confirm a real `MoveCmd` was accepted and the ship arrived. `git diff 961a9d4a..9e920c18 --
src/app/src/viewer.cpp src/app/src/opening_ui.cpp src/app/src/opening_ui.hpp src/app/src/dev_script.cpp
src/app/src/ship_motion.cpp src/app/src/ship_layer.cpp src/sim/src/` is empty: PLAY-LIVE-1a touches none of the
input-routing, ownership or ship-command files, so a run without `--rules` is exactly main's own code path; **PLAY-
LIVE-1a is not involved.**

**The one mechanism the code and its own tests already show can silently drop a real order, found by reading
(not reproduced live — the scripted input below always has zero travel, so it cannot exercise this path):**
`OpeningUi::pointer_up` (`opening_ui.cpp`) requires the press-to-release travel to stay under `kClickSlop` (5 px,
`opening_ui.hpp`) or the gesture is a pan, not a click, and `pointer_up` returns an empty `UiResult` — no command,
no message, nothing for `update_title()` to show. `opening_ui_test.cpp`'s own "a right-button drag of 20 pixels: a
pan" case proves this silently empty result. `kClickSlop` and this logic are unchanged since the opening's own
first commit (`12af6def`), before the working 2026-11-03 playtest (`8cae6f71`), so this is not a regression and
not PLAY-LIVE-1a's — but it is the only place in the code where a real order can vanish with literally nothing
shown, matching "I can select but cannot command the ship ... it won't move at all" better than any refusal
message would (every refusal the code can give — land, outside the world, not yours — sets `ui.message()`, which
`opening_facts`/the title surfaces).

**Why I stopped instead of fixing it:** the scripted reproduction cannot move the pointer during a press by a
sub-pixel amount a real mouse does automatically; whether the owner's actual click travelled ≥5 device pixels
(an ordinary right-click's natural hand movement, more likely at a higher density/DPI scale than this PC's own
1.00 or under a game-type gaming mouse's own click-and-settle behaviour) is not something this reproduction can
settle one way or the other. Per the packet: no guess-fix.

Gates: no source file changed; hosted CI on the docs-only push (report below).

NOT_RUN: `tools/test/run_selected.py` (no code change to gate); the WSL ASan build (same reason); a real Windows
desktop session with the owner's own display/mouse settings (not available here).

Decisions and reasoning:
- Treated main's unchanged files as direct evidence for main's own behaviour, rather than building a second
  worktree at `961a9d4a`: `git diff 961a9d4a..9e920c18` over every file plausibly on the ship-order path is empty,
  so a run on `9e920c18`'s own binary without `--rules` is bit-for-bit main's own code path.
- Did not add an artificial travel-injecting dev-script verb to force-reproduce the `kClickSlop` path: it would
  prove the already-proven unit-test behaviour again, not settle whether that is what the owner hit, and the
  packet asks not to guess a fix (or, by the same reasoning, a cause) without evidence from the owner's own
  conditions.

## ZOOM-MEASURE-1 — a camera sweep that measures what the owner sees — 2026-11-13 — READY FOR REVIEW

Base `main` `961a9d4a`, branch `task/ZOOM-MEASURE-1`, head `f7e23dca`. Measurement only, no renderer
behaviour change.

**Counters added** to `bench_frame --zoom-sweep` (extended, not a new tool): per frame, read straight
from `GpuStats` (the window's own per-second report's source) — `chunks_missing` (non-ready visible
chunks), `stand_in_parts` (stand-in draws), `chunks_fading` (dissolves), `open_sea_chunks`
(placeholder draws), `fluid_fade<1` (inside a wave cross-fade) and `fluid_windows` (wave switches,
summed as positive steps so a mid-run counter reset can't underflow); printed per level and as one
overall line, alongside the existing busy-time percentiles and a new "frames > 2 ms" column (the
500 Hz budget). `<file>` now also accepts a `.txt` fixed map or `.json` ship-start manifest, through
`app::load_play`/`app::load_opening` then `app::load_placed_scene` — the real window's own loaders,
no placement logic duplicated.

**Sweep profiles:** `legs` (today's continuous zoom, default, unchanged), `wheel` (discrete
8-notch/s steps, off-centre anchor, no pan), `pan` (one fixed level, a 1200 px/s reversing pan, no
zoom change), `zoompan` (legs' continuous zoom at the fast pan speed). `--zoom-sweep-warm` (an
unmeasured pass first, same `FrameRenderer`) + `--zoom-sweep-skip n` (drops the measured pass's own
first n frames) build the "everything resident" control.

**Baseline** (RTX 4090, 2560x1369, enhanced water unless noted; full table in
`docs/perf/README.md`): none of lan5.txt/ship-start x legs/wheel/pan/zoompan reaches 0 — e.g. lan5.txt
legs: 431/12000 non-ready frames, 26616 stand-in draws, 13304 dissolves, 329 frames > 2ms; wheel and
zoompan are worse (593–881 non-ready, up to 45485 stand-ins) than pan (57, 37) — a fast pan at a
fixed level misses far less than any zoom change. Original water (no wave sim) still shows 537
non-ready frames — the failure is chunk readiness (RC1), not the water (RC3). 1280x800 is much
better than 2560x1369 (84 vs 431 non-ready) — smaller view, smaller grid. The Radeon iGPU (1280x800)
has fewer misses (10) but a far worse worst frame (37.1 ms, an offscreen-sea-target resize) —
RC4's separate story. This is a representative subset of the full map x water x resolution x
adapter x mode cross product; see Decisions below for the scope cut and why.

**The contract** (`tools/test/zoom_sweep_contract.py`): 0 non-ready, 0 stand-ins, 0 dissolves, 0
open-sea draws, 2 ms busy budget (4 warm-up frames excluded). Fails today on every real profile
above, not relaxed. The **"everything resident" control** (camera truly at rest, warm cache): every
readiness counter is exactly 0 — proving the criteria are reachable — but 2 of 1980 frames (0.1%)
still exceed the busy budget, stable across reruns with nothing else on the machine: GPU/driver
submission jitter (RC4), not a readiness failure, and not hidden — reported as a separate finding.
Not wired into CTest: a correctly-failing test would turn `gate` red for every commit until
ZOOM-SMOOTH-1; run manually for this evidence (`docs/perf/README.md` has the exact commands).

**The window-event hitch:** `ANNO_VIEW_HITCH_MS=5`, a real window, manually dragged and
maximised/restored. A 106.0 ms hitch with **96.7 ms inside "handling window events"**
(`events_ms_`, the `while (SDL_PollEvent(&e)) handle(e);` loop) confirms zoom-smoothness.md §5's
suspected mechanism directly: SDL's blocking poll inside Windows' modal move/resize loop. A second,
17.9 ms hitch on restore-from-maximised spent 15.98 ms in "surface configure" (the swapchain
rebuild). Not fixed here.

Gates: `cmake --build --preset msvc` warning-free. clang-format 23.1.3 clean.
`python -I tools/test/workflow_test.py`: 24 tests, OK (`tools/test` touched). `anno_app_tests`
(MSVC Release, game files — `bench_frame` links `anno_app_core`, no test suite of its own):
`selected=267 executed=265 failed=0 skipped=2(opt-in) sanitizer_lines=0 VERDICT: PASS`. CI on
`f7e23dca`: `cpp (macos-clang)`/`cpp (linux-clang-asan)` failed Clang's `-Werror` on a set-but-unused
summary variable (fixed in `738b0f71`, printed as a second busy-time column instead of discarded;
confirmed clean against `tools/check_unix_warnings.sh`, GCC 13 + Clang 18, with and without GPU).
CI on `738b0f71` (run `43436856818`): every job green, `gate` included.

NOT_RUN: the full map x water x resolution x adapter x mode cross product (scope cut, below); the
WSL ASan build (no code in `src/app`/`src/render`/`src/sim` changed — `src/tools/bench_frame` only,
covered by the app-test gate above as the nearest shared-library check); ZOOM-SMOOTH-1's fix; ADR
0007 (orchestrator's); the full WSL gate and game-file run (orchestrator's, at merge).

Decisions and reasoning:
- Ran a representative subset, not the full 2 maps x 2 water x 2 resolutions x 2 adapters x 4 modes
  (32+ runs): the primary 4090/2560x1369/enhanced matrix across both maps and all 4 modes (8 runs),
  plus one spot-check each for 1280x800, original water and the iGPU, chosen to show every factor
  the packet names still matters without exhausting the packet's own time budget.
- `pan` mode holds ONE level for the whole sweep (the leg's own starting level), not the leg's own
  `from`/`to` range: an earlier version still crossed 4 different levels between legs even at pan
  speed 0, which is not a camera-at-rest control at all.
- Wave switches are summed as positive steps across frames in time order, not `last − first`: the
  simulation's own counter is not guaranteed never to reset mid-sweep, and a `std::uint64_t`
  subtraction wraps instead of going negative.
- Did not wire `zoom_sweep_contract.py` into CTest: a test that is meant to fail until a future
  packet lands would turn `gate` red on every commit between now and ZOOM-SMOOTH-1, which is a
  worse outcome than running it manually for this packet's own evidence.
- Used the project's own `app::load_play`/`app::load_opening` for the new file types rather than
  reimplementing manifest/fixed-map parsing in `bench_frame`: the real window already resolves
  island templates and placement, and bench_frame only needs the resulting `render::Scene`.

QUESTIONs: none required; the fix is explicitly not this packet's.

## DEPTH-INTEGRATE-1 — buildings sit in the ground and the water; the sea at the original's level — 2026-11-13 — READY FOR REVIEW

Base `main` `f9e6ea0c`, merged `origin/task/W4-depth-1` `5eaef168` into `task/DEPTH-INTEGRATE-1`, head `10e1a3ce`
(merge `a6880348` + test fix `3fd866d7` + playtest-card doc `10e1a3ce`).

**The merge.** `frame.{cpp,hpp}`, `gpu.{cpp,hpp}`, `gpu.wgsl`, `gpu_test.cpp` and `iso.md` auto-merged (both sides
changed them since 2026-11-04). Three append-only doc conflicts as predicted (`open-questions.md`,
`docs/orchestration/REPORTS.md`, `docs/perf/README.md`): git's 3-way diff matched unrelated identical-looking
text across entries on two of the three (a shared "Owner decision" line and a shared "**Acceptance table.**"
header format used by several entries), so I rebuilt each file from the branch's own isolated diff
(`git diff <merge-base> origin/task/W4-depth-1 -- <file>`) against today's HEAD rather than trust the markers —
confirmed clean, nothing dropped from either side.

**Proving the merge found a real regression:** two synthetic river-mask tests
(`river_flow_test.cpp`, "the shipped criteria on the tile grid", "a bridge never crosses sea and is deep enough
to carry flow") never set `IslandWater::shore_height` and so picked up the new `kShoreHeight` default (26.5); their
terrain heights (24, calibrated against the old 16.5) then also read as plain sea by elevation, contaminating the
river-specific classification they check. Fixed by pinning `iw.shore_height = 16.5F` explicitly in both fixtures
(an earlier attempt that raised the height literals instead left one case passing but changed the other's bridge
count from 1 to 3 — an unintended ripple into unrelated logic; reverted). Both pass now, and the fix is its own
commit (`3fd866d7`) with the mechanism in its message.

**The branch's claims, re-proven on today's main:** `anno_render_tests`/`anno_render_gpu_tests`/`anno_app_tests`
(MSVC Release, game files, RTX 4090): `selected=591 executed=586 failed=0 skipped=3(opt-in) sanitizer_lines=0
VERDICT: PASS` — 5 of the 591 showed `[anno-test memory] refused ... low-memory stop` once each across two runs
(never the same 5 twice), each confirmed passing alone (one via an incidental full-suite rerun, 2582/2582). This
includes the GPU=CPU depth corpus (`chunk draw lists replay...`, 2742 chunks) and the Rust-reference digest check
(`scene renders match the recorded digests`) — `--depth off`'s digests, unchanged. `kShoreHeight = 26.5F` (merged
from the branch) is the only digest-affecting default this packet moves; nothing needed re-pinning beyond what the
branch already pinned. WSL `-O1` ASan, render+app lanes: `selected=508 executed=503 failed=0 skipped=3(opt-in)
sanitizer_lines=0 VERDICT: PASS` (same 2 refusals, confirmed passing alone). Radeon iGPU, `anno_render_gpu_tests`:
`selected=117 executed=117 failed=0`.

**The pictures** (candidate A, seat 0, sailed and founded at `(255,138)` per `ship-opening-playtest.md` step 3,
CPU renderer — the GPU path's screenshot is a desktop copy that needs a visible, unlocked screen, which an
unattended run can't guarantee; same depth/scene code either way), in
`C:\Users\altin\Pictures\anno-review\DEPTH-INTEGRATE-1\`: `kontor_depth-on_shore-26.5_default.png` (this build's
own default), `-off_shore-26.5`, `-on_shore-16.5`, `-off_shore-16.5`. With depth on, the Kontor's piles and its
dock end short, embedded in the sloping bank; with depth off the same piles stand full-length on top of the sand.

## FISHER-1a — state-free water and search geometry (2026-11-14)

Branch task/FISHER-1a; new worktree from main f54e36f0; packet/owner rules read at board 3a87b3bf.
Implementation d9fdbff1; no reviewer agents; independent orchestrator review pending.
API in fisher.hpp: fisher_corner(span<const u8>, u32 W,H,cx,cy) -> optional<u8>; fisher_cell(array<u8,4>, u8 threshold) -> FisherCell{mean,walkable_water,goal_mask}; fisher_cell_at(span<const u8>, u32 W,H,x,y, u8 threshold) -> optional<FisherCell>; fisher_search_rect(u16 x,y, u32 W,H,r) -> optional<FisherSearchRect{u16 x,y;u8 width,height}>.
Corner lookup copies W × H samples unchanged; logical right/bottom edges are zero; no allocation. Wrong sample length/outside coordinates return nullopt; cell coordinates must be inside W × H.
Threshold: kFisherWaterThreshold = 32, a documented function parameter default, not SimConfig/state. AnnoWelt.dll 0x100e34dc / 0x1008fea0 / 0x1008ff00; sourced lint allowance, no content limit.
Unsigned four-corner mean divides by 4; water iff mean < threshold; goal mask 511 otherwise, 0 below.
Rectangle follows 0x10059210–0x10059398: origin wraps modulo 65536, extent modulo 256, never clamps. Negative origin -6 becomes 65530; extent 256 becomes 0. Widened arithmetic, no map/radius cap; zero footprint returns nullopt. No scheduler wiring, World member, extension tag or identity change.
Vectors executed: sea_cell 6, corner_grid 5, search_rect 5; 33 other records skipped by explicit name. Border means 31 and 32 ran; unit cases cover threshold 33, singleton/borders, invalid input and wrap.

## SHORE-2 — the sea's edge follows the terrain at the original's plane — 2026-11-14 — READY FOR REVIEW

Base `origin/task/DEPTH-INTEGRATE-1` `eff68d5e`, branch `task/SHORE-2`, merged `origin/main` `f54e36f0` (clean,
no conflicts in the branch's own files) as `84d1d323`, then a clang-format fix as `8a7b36dc`.

**The trace, time-boxed to about an hour** (`docs/re/annowelt.md`, new subsection; `docs/open-questions.md`
OQ-026): the chunk sea-bit writer is `0x1009ebf0`. For a corner belonging to an island it gates the bit on a
per-GFXID vtable query (slot `+0x13c`), not on the corner's own height; only a corner outside every island
(tile-id `0xFF`) tests height, via `0x100b5dc0` against a constant near the sea anchor `0x100e3a1c`. Neither
`0x100b5dc0`'s bound nor `+0x13c`'s predicate resolved in the time-box — narrows, does not close, OQ-026.

**The rule as built** (`src/render/src/sea.cpp`, `IslandWater::build`): the packet's sanctioned fallback, labelled
as an approximation, not the traced rule. A chunk holds sea if any of its tiles has a corner below
`Scene::shore_height`, replacing the fixed `average ≤ 19` classifier (`kLandAverage`) that ignored `shore_height`
entirely. `kLandAverage` itself is untouched — it stays the land classifier used elsewhere (`frame_projection.cpp`,
`legal_workload.cpp`), unrelated to this bit.

**GPU = CPU:** structural, not measured per-pixel — `IslandWater::build` has exactly one caller
(`scene.cpp:942`) and its `sea_chunk` output feeds both the CPU and GPU chunk-build paths from the same struct;
no separate GPU-side change was needed or made. `--depth off` and `--shore 16.5`/`--shore 26.5` still select as
before; the water-field empty-cell proof (`iso.md`) uses the same bit and needed no condition change.

**Coverage table (item 3):** NOT_RUN — recomputing it against the original needs a live original/Wine capture
session, not available this session.

NOT_RUN: steps 2-6 (the byte memory budget, resident coarse levels, the zoom-out ring, the GPU upload share,
rate-limited eviction) and step 9's tests that depend on them; the Radeon iGPU GPU gate (reasoned above);
WSL ASan.

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Scope cut after reading the packet in full.** Steps 2-6 are one tightly-coupled redesign (a byte budget
  spanning the CPU chunk cache and the GPU's planes/pool/prefetch together, resident-level selection by that
  budget, a new zoom-out ring ordered by estimated time-to-visible, routing the ring and resident levels into
  the compositor's upload-ahead even while a visible chunk waits, and rate-limited eviction with watermarks),
  not five independent small changes. The review that rewrote this packet already flagged real risk inside
  it: B2 (today's prefetch gate, `!waiting && uploads == 0`, is exactly what step 5 must change, inside
  `gpu.cpp`'s most delicate scheduling code) and B3 (moving GPU releases risks priority inversion with the
  existing reaper, and wgpu may destroy resources inside `queue submit` regardless, a wgpu-core-version-
  specific point the packet itself says must be checked, not assumed). Attempting all of it in this one
  sitting, without the owner's or a reviewer's eyes on intermediate states (the project's own practice for
  work this size, e.g. SHORE-2's multi-round review), risked landing a plausible-looking but under-verified
  rewrite of safety-critical rendering scheduling. Shipping steps 1, 7 and 8 to a solid, gated, tested
  standard and stopping there, per the packet's own "stop and report" rule, serves the evidence-only bar
  better than a rushed pass at the rest.
- **Proposed split:** steps 2+3 (the byte budget and resident-by-budget) as one packet, since 3 cannot be
  measured without 2; step 4 (the ring) next, since it needs the same budget-aware residency to reason about
  what's already resident; step 5 (GPU upload share) last and on its own, given B2/B3's flagged risk,
  possibly after checking wgpu-core's pinned-version behaviour the review named as unverified; step 6
  (eviction rate limits) can ride with whichever of 2/3 lands first, since it's the same trim() path. Step 9's
  tests split the same way.
- Kept step 7 off the `baseline: ...` line `zoom_sweep_contract.py` parses by a fixed regex, adding the
  chunks-step p99/max only to the per-level table, so the existing contract needed no change.
- `--readiness-only` instead of reusing `--control` to add a gate, so the documented manual recipe in
  `docs/perf/README.md` (which still wants the full busy-time picture) is unaffected.
- Did not relax the busy-time threshold to make `--control` pass outright, per the review's own instruction;
  deferred that decision to ZOOM-SMOOTH-3, whose charge is exactly the window-thread busy-time story.

QUESTIONs: should steps 2-6 be split as above into separate packets, or dispatched as one larger packet to
this same branch? Either way, the branch currently holds no behaviour change to any renderer or GPU code —
only the proof harness, a report-only metric and an opt-in test — so it is safe to land as is, or to keep
open for the next packet to build on.

**READY FOR REVIEW.**

## ZOOM-SMOOTH-1b — the chunk memory budget, resident levels and rate-limited eviction — READY FOR REVIEW (task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1b, from task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1 `e8dcb7cf`, head `2f5ab906`)

Steps 2, 3 and 6 of the packet, as scoped by the split review. `gpu.cpp`'s prefetch gate (B2)
and the ring (step 4) were not touched, as instructed; nothing needed to.

**The budget (step 2):** `ChunkMemoryBudget`/`default_chunk_budget` (`frame.hpp`/`frame.cpp`):
discrete 4 GiB, integrated/unknown an eighth of system RAM (floored 256 MiB, capped 2 GiB),
software the floor alone — as `GpuLimits::atlas_budget_mb` already sizes by adapter kind, since
WebGPU reports no memory size. Halved against the GPU holding the same chunks again (no
separate GPU-side counter or eviction: the compositor already drops its copy as soon as the CPU
one is evicted, `gpu.cpp sync_chunks`). `FrameRenderer::cache_bytes()` is the running total, kept
incrementally at every cache insert/replace/erase (not summed each frame); a test checks it
against the existing O(n) `cached_bytes()`. 0 (the default) is unbudgeted — today's exact
count-based behaviour, so no existing test or digest changed. Viewer option
`ANNO_VIEW_CHUNK_BUDGET_MB=<n>` (0 = off); bench_frame's `--chunk-budget-mb` mirrors it (system
RAM unknown there: bench_frame does not link SDL3).

**Resident levels (step 3):** `is_resident_level` — a level is resident if it fits
`resident_level_chunks` (kept as a floor, "the original 16-chunk residency stays reachable") or
the budget's resident share (half the budget by default), measured against a conservative flat
per-chunk estimate (`kChunkByteEstimate`, the same figure `gpu.hpp`'s plane pool already uses)
so a level marked resident never turns out not to fit once built. `prewarm_far_levels` now fills
every idle worker thread at once (`prewarm_targets_`, a vector, was a single `optional`) instead
of one chunk at a time (review finding S3), and runs in every session (viewer), not only the
ship-start opening.

**Rate-limited eviction (step 6):** `trim()`'s byte-budget path evicts the least relevant
candidate first (the opposite end of the same priority order the count-based path already
used), stopped by a 0.9/0.75 high/low watermark band and a per-call `max_evict_bytes_per_frame`
cap, so a large overshoot spreads over several frames instead of freeing all at once.

**Tests:** `cache_bytes` vs `cached_bytes` agreement; `default_chunk_budget`'s three adapter
cases, floor and cap; `is_resident_level` widening and narrowing with the floor and the budget
(game files, the island's known level sizes); eviction capped at `max_evict_bytes_per_frame`,
spread over two calls (synthetic chunks, no game files). The existing `derived_freshness` prewarm
suite (fill, stale rebuild, a failed target not blocking the rest) passed unchanged against the
new multi-target fill, 12/12.

**Measured (the fixed sweep, lan5, 2560x1369, enhanced, 6 s/leg, 4090; budget on, its default):**
before → after, from the ZOOM-SMOOTH-1 baseline:
- legs: non-ready 193→46, stand-in 22484→6576, dissolves 14472→5072, open-sea 1922→1634, busy
  p99 2.70→2.42 ms, frames>2ms 353→234.
- wheel: non-ready 153→28, stand-in 24950→5583, dissolves 14921→4422, open-sea 1901→1435, busy
  p99 2.90→2.28 ms, frames>2ms 374→177.
- pan: non-ready 47→25, stand-in 17→0, dissolves 1346→868, open-sea 1979→1300, busy p99
  1.61→1.91 ms, **frames>2ms 30→96 (worse)**.
- zoompan: non-ready 241→35, stand-in 34448→16596, dissolves 15803→7072, open-sea 1954→1391,
  busy p99 2.44→2.38 ms, frames>2ms 264→218.
- Radeon iGPU wheel, 1280x800: non-ready 13→7, stand-in 275→217, dissolves 144→105, open-sea
  45→39, **frames>2ms 28→41 (worse)**; max frame time 279→306 ms (the same resize-type outlier
  noise both runs, not content).

Readiness (non-ready, stand-in, dissolves, open-sea) improved on every mode and both adapters,
often by 50-80%, from the resident levels and the wider working set the budget now allows. The
busy-time tail got worse on pan and the iGPU, not better: pan's own `chunks` step stayed small
(p99 0.307 ms, max 0.736 ms, from the per-level table), so the extra frames over 2 ms are the
cost of filling every idle worker with background prewarm builds throughout the pan, not of the
window thread's own planning. Cache memory on the 4090 run reached 3,678 MB (max, legs/pan
tables), under the 4 GiB default budget as expected. Not claiming the packet's 0-on-every-counter
target: that is 1d's (the GPU upload share) and the ring's (1c) to reach.

**Gates.** MSVC Release, game files, render+app: `COUNTS: selected=536 executed=530 failed=3
empty=0 skipped=3 (opt-in=3) incomplete=0 sanitizer_lines=0` / `VERDICT: FAIL failed tests`
(`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1b-render-app-1.txt`) — all 3 confirmed `[anno-test memory] refused ...
reason=low-memory`; each passed alone (`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1b-solo-1.txt` through `-3.txt`,
each `VERDICT: PASS`). GPU, 4090: `COUNTS: selected=117 executed=117 failed=0 VERDICT: PASS`
(`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1b-gpu-4090.txt`); the Radeon iGPU gate was not rerun (no GPU code
changed; the iGPU sweep numbers above exercise the same binary). WSL `-Werror` check
(`tools/check_unix_warnings.sh`): clean except the same pre-existing, unrelated
`src/sim/tests/extensions_test.cpp` failure already present on `task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1`.
`clang-format --dry-run --Werror` flagged several lines across the changed files; fixed in
place, rebuilt, retested (unaffected — `apply_frame_config`/`cache_bytes`/`default_chunk_budget`/
`trim` tests all still pass).

Pushing `89c12221` failed hosted CI's `cpp (linux-gcc)`/`cpp (linux-gcc-release)` jobs (MSVC had
not flagged it): `-Wsign-conversion` on the budget's megabyte-to-byte math, mixing
`std::uint64_t` (`unsigned long` on this GCC/Linux target) with `1024ULL`-suffixed literals (a
different, same-width type) in the viewer's `ANNO_VIEW_CHUNK_BUDGET_MB` override and
bench_frame's `--chunk-budget-mb`. Fixed by using `std::uint64_t{1024}` consistently, verified
with the WSL `-Werror` check again (clean, same pre-existing unrelated failure), rebuilt on
MSVC, committed as `93bcb57a`, pushed.

NOT_RUN: steps 4 and 5 (the ring, the GPU upload share) and their step-9 tests, per the split;
the Radeon iGPU CTest gate (reasoned above); WSL ASan.

Decisions and reasoning:
- Used a flat, conservative per-chunk byte estimate for residency decisions (matching the GPU's
  own plane-pool constant) rather than a real built total, so a level can never flap in and out
  of residency once it is actually built — at the cost of under-using the budget on sea-heavy
  levels, which the real `cached_bytes()` still reports accurately for everything already built.
- Did not add a live GPU-side byte counter: the compositor already drops a chunk's planes as
  soon as its CPU copy is evicted (no independent GPU eviction exists to drive), so the "count
  both sides" requirement is honoured by sizing `default_chunk_budget` at half of what the
  adapter/RAM can spare, not by duplicating the CPU's bookkeeping on the GPU side.
- Reported pan's and the iGPU's worse busy-time tail rather than only the readiness wins: the
  packet's own instruction is "report better, equal or worse per level," and the `chunks` step's
  own timing rules out the window thread's planning as the cause, pointing instead at
  contention from the now much more aggressive background prewarm fill — a genuine trade-off for
  1c/1d or a future tuning pass to weigh, not a result to understate.
- Left `gpu.cpp` untouched, as instructed, since steps 2/3/6 needed no change there: the existing
  "a visible chunk's build and the CPU cache evicting it" contract already keeps the GPU side in
  sync without any new code.

QUESTIONs: is a 0.5 resident/working-set split the right default, given pan's own regression
suggests the working set (not the resident levels) is where most of 1b's actual readiness win
came from? A future packet (1c, 1d, or a tuning pass) may want real data before changing it.

**READY FOR REVIEW.**

## ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c — F1-F3 fixed, the pan/iGPU "regression" corrected — READY FOR REVIEW (task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c, from task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1b `d71bbfbb`, head `8f4b6ebe`)

F1, F2 and F3 are done and tested. Step 4 (the zoom-out ring) is **not started** — see Decisions. The
pan/iGPU busy-time finding from the 1b review turned out not to be a code regression; see below, first,
since it reframes the whole packet.

**The pan/iGPU "regression": corrected, not removed by a code change.** The review's instruction was to
measure the cause before fixing it. Measuring it is what found there was nothing in 1b's code to fix:

- **Isolating the resident-level prewarm** (the review's own suspect) with the new `--resident-prewarm off`:
  pan's frames>2ms went 96 → 92. Capping the fill at 1 target (the pre-1b width) instead of every worker:
  90. None of these come close to the recorded 1-baseline's 30.
- **The decisive check: rerunning the original, unmodified `task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1` `bench_frame` binary, right
  now, on pan.** Three runs: 102, 127, 105 frames>2ms — nowhere near its own recorded 30, on code that has
  not changed since that number was written down. `legs` on the same unmodified binary reproduces closely
  (350 vs its recorded 353) and `wheel`/`zoompan` likewise (373/317 vs 374/264) — only `pan`'s particular
  camera path is this volatile on this machine right now; it is not a general drift the other modes would
  also show.
- **The shipped 1c code, same session, three runs:** 100, 102, 106 — indistinguishable from the unmodified
  binary's own 102/127/105, if anything slightly tighter. Pan is not worse than the baseline measured today;
  the 30 recorded in ZOOM-SMOOTH-1's own REPORTS entry was not reproducible even by that entry's own
  unmodified binary, on this run of this machine.
- **The iGPU wheel case is different: it reproduced.** The unmodified 1a binary gave 22 frames>2ms today
  (close to its recorded 28); 1b's code (before F2) gave 33. That is a real, modest regression on the iGPU
  specifically - and F2 (below) fixes it outright: with the real system RAM instead of the 256 MiB floor,
  the same 1c code gives 12 frames>2ms, non-ready 3, stand-in draws 0, dissolves 26 - better than either
  number, because the iGPU sweep had never measured the budget the viewer actually gives it until now.

**F1 (resident share, cumulative):** `is_resident_level` checked each derived level's own cost against the
*whole* resident share; since each derived level has about a quarter the chunks of the one below, the
levels together could take up to about 4/3 of the share, and none that individually fit was ever trimmed -
the working set was then left with less than its own share. Now gives the share out cumulatively, farthest
(coarsest) level first. New test (`src/render/tests/derived_freshness_test.cpp`): a budget sized so the
island's two derived levels (8 and 24 chunks) each fit alone but not together (32 > a 30-chunk share)
confirms only the farther one is resident now, not both.

**F2 (the iGPU's real RAM):** `bench_frame` passed `system_ram_bytes = 0` to `default_chunk_budget` (it
links `anno_app_core`, not `anno_app_sdl`, so `SDL_GetSystemRAM` isn't available there), so a non-discrete
adapter sat at the 256 MiB floor while the viewer gets an eighth of real RAM, capped at 2 GiB - the B1 kind
of mismatch again. `system_ram_bytes()` reads it directly (`GlobalMemoryStatusEx` on Windows, `sysconf` on
POSIX). Rerunning the iGPU sweep with it is the number quoted above.

**F3 (the eviction cap):** `default_chunk_budget` left `max_evict_bytes_per_frame` at 0 (unbounded), so
step 6's rate limit existed but nothing in the viewer turned it on. Set to 64 chunks' worth (the same order
of magnitude as the original `spare_chunks` default) rather than just asserting the watermark band alone is
enough.

**Measured (fixed sweep, lan5, 6 s/leg, same-session before/after on this head's build), 4090:**

| mode | before (1a, same session) | after (1c) |
|---|---|---|
| legs | non-ready 224, stand-in 14987, dissolves 8560, open-sea 1617, >2ms 350 | non-ready 35, stand-in 6032, dissolves 4533, open-sea 1544, >2ms 201 |
| wheel | non-ready 103, stand-in 18937, dissolves 10546, open-sea 1352, >2ms 373 | non-ready 31, stand-in 5332, dissolves 4618, open-sea 1462, >2ms 162 |
| pan | non-ready 24-41 (3 runs), stand-in 0, dissolves 759-963, open-sea 1174-1534, >2ms 90-127 (3 runs) | non-ready 24-36 (3 runs), stand-in 0, dissolves 828-921, open-sea 1305-1398, >2ms 100-106 (3 runs) |
| zoompan | non-ready 71, stand-in 23912, dissolves 10306, open-sea 1525, >2ms 317 | non-ready 37, stand-in 14519, dissolves 6288, open-sea 1406, >2ms 189 |
| iGPU wheel, 1280x800 | non-ready 15, stand-in 266, dissolves 146, open-sea 47, >2ms 22 | non-ready 3, stand-in 0, dissolves 26, open-sea 44, >2ms 12 |

Readiness improved on every mode and both adapters, same as 1b reported. Busy-time is now equal (pan,
within run-to-run noise) or better (legs/wheel/zoompan/iGPU) everywhere - the explicit landing requirement
("pan's frames over 2 ms must be no worse than the 1-baseline") is met by the corrected measurement, not by
a code change to pan's own path.

**Gates.** MSVC Release, game files, render+app: `COUNTS: selected=537 executed=534 failed=0 empty=0
skipped=3 (opt-in=3) incomplete=0 sanitizer_lines=0` / `VERDICT: PASS`
(`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1c-render-app-1.txt`) - clean, no refusals. GPU, 4090: `COUNTS: selected=117
executed=117 failed=0 VERDICT: PASS` (`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1c-gpu-4090.txt`). The Radeon iGPU CTest gate
was not rerun (no GPU code changed; the iGPU sweep numbers above exercise the same binary, as in 1b). WSL
`-Werror` check: clean except the same pre-existing, unrelated `extensions_test.cpp` failure. Caught and
fixed along the way: a GCC/Clang-only (`-Wimplicit-int-float-conversion`/`-Wconversion`) sign/precision bug
in the new F1 test's own assertion (`std::size_t * double` without an explicit cast) that MSVC did not flag.

NOT_RUN: step 4 (the zoom-out ring) and its step-9 tests - see Decisions; the Radeon iGPU CTest gate
(reasoned above); WSL ASan.

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Measured before fixing**, per the review's own instruction, rather than assuming either suggested cause
  (prewarm contention, or the budget's working-set size) and patching around it. Both were tested directly
  (`--resident-prewarm off`, a capped-to-1 fill, a small `--chunk-budget-mb`) and neither reproduced the
  reported gap; only reverifying the *unmodified* 1a binary against its own recorded number, right now,
  revealed that the 30-frame pan baseline itself could not be reproduced. Reporting an invented fix for a
  regression that measurement shows does not exist would have been worse than reporting the correction.
- **Kept the diagnostic flag** (`--resident-prewarm`) rather than deleting it once the diagnosis was done:
  it is small, real, and useful for whoever next needs to isolate the resident-level prewarm's own cost
  (1d, the ring, or a future tuning pass).
- **Deferred step 4, the zoom-out ring.** "Order by estimated time until visible, from the zoom direction
  and the pan velocity" needs a zoom-direction signal `FrameRenderer` does not currently track (velocity is
  pan-only by design, per `motion_centre`'s own doc: a zoom's own anchor-driven shift is deliberately
  excluded from it). Building that signal, the ring's own geometry (a new scale-about-anchor view function,
  since `zoomed_view_at` only jumps between zoom *groups*, not scales within one), and the "pan must not be
  starved by it" invariant together are a correctness-sensitive feature on their own, not a quick addition
  on top of the regression investigation this packet turned into. Attempting it in the remaining time risked
  either rushing the starvation guarantee or the ordering, both explicitly called out as required. Proposed
  as 1d, or its own packet, with the zoom-direction signal as its first sub-step.
- **F3's cap is a measured default** (64 chunks, matching `spare_chunks`' own order of magnitude) rather
  than an argument that the watermark band alone suffices: the band and the per-call cap address different
  things (steady-state trim frequency vs. a single burst's size, e.g. right after a lowered
  `ANNO_VIEW_CHUNK_BUDGET_MB`), so asserting one makes the other unnecessary would have been the kind of
  unevidenced claim the project's evidence contract rules out.

QUESTIONs: should step 4 (the ring) be its own packet (1c-ring) ahead of 1d, given 1d (the GPU upload share)
doesn't depend on it, or should it ride with 1d since both touch "what's urgently wanted during a zoom"? The
0.5 resident/working-set split question from 1b's QUESTION is still open and now has real same-session
numbers to inform it once the ring exists to use them.

**READY FOR REVIEW.**

## ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c2 — the zoom-out ring — READY FOR REVIEW (task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c2, from task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c `96c00844`, head `b066612b`)

All four of 1c's released steps, done and tested: the zoom-direction signal, the ring's geometry, the ring
itself wired into the existing priority ordering, and the starvation invariant as a test.

**1. The zoom-direction signal.** `FrameRenderer::zoom_direction` (`frame.hpp`, default 0): negative while
zooming out, positive while zooming in, 0 at rest. Kept apart from `velocity()` on purpose — `velocity()` is
pan-only by design (`motion_centre`'s own doc: the viewer sets the camera minus the zoom's own anchor-driven
displacement before each update, so a pure zoom never moves it), and the ring below needs to tell "the camera
is panning" apart from "the camera is zooming out", which a single combined signal could not. Set by the
viewer (`frames_.zoom_direction = zoom_target_ - zoom_now_;`, next to the existing `zoom_anchor` assignment)
and by `bench_frame`'s `zoom_sweep()` (`fr.zoom_direction = s.target - s.now;`, from the `ZoomState` already
tracked there).

**2. The ring's geometry.** `ring_view_at(view, anchor, group, levels, coarse_margin = 0.95)` (`frame.hpp`/
`frame.cpp`): scales `view` about `anchor`, within the *same* group, to the area the composed grid would show
just before `group + 1` takes over (scale factor `tile_w(group) / (coarse_margin * tile_w(group + 1))` per
axis, `tile_h` for y; always > 1, since a finer group has the larger on-screen tile). The anchor's *fractional*
position within `view` is preserved in the returned rect — `zoomed_view_at` only preserves a pixel *offset*,
which assumes the view's size is unchanged; here the view itself grows, so the fraction is what stays fixed.
Returns `view` unchanged at the coarsest level (`group + 1 >= levels.size()`): nothing left to ring toward.

**3. The ring itself.** Wired into `FrameRenderer::plan_margin` as a fourth priority class (`rank = 3`,
strictly after the visible view = 0, the same-group pan lookahead = 1, and the neighbouring-group views = 2),
through the same `add()`/priority-queue mechanism the other three classes already use, so `plan_jobs`'s
`kPlanKeys` cutoff drops ring candidates first if the cap is ever hit. Only triggered when `zoom_anchor` is set
and `zoom_direction < 0`; added at the *same* group as the current view (the ring is "what a zoom-out to the
edge of the current level would need", not a derived or neighbouring level).

**4. The invariant as a test.** New case in `derived_freshness_test.cpp`: a multi-chunk (1536×1536) view with
`zoom_anchor` at its centre and `zoom_direction = -1`, run for 60 rounds of `update_chunks`/`wait_idle` with one
worker. Each round checks that any chunk found inside `ring_view_at`'s own area but outside
`visible_chunks(view) ∪ margin_keys() ∪ adjacent_keys()` arrives only once that non-ring set is itself complete
(`REQUIRE`), and that the ring actually produces such a chunk at least once across the 60 rounds (`CHECK`).
**First attempt failed** (`CHECK(saw_ring_key)` false): the detection loop scanned derived levels
(`g >= built_count()`), but the ring (step 3) requests chunks at the *same* group as the view — a built level,
not a derived one — so it was looking in the wrong place. A second issue, found at the same time: a 512×512
(one-chunk) view's ring, at the typical group-0/group-1 tile ratio (~2.1×), never grows past the pan
lookahead's own unconditional one-chunk border, so there was no ring-exclusive content to find regardless of
where the test looked. Fixed both: the test's detection now checks group-0 keys inside
`ring_view_at(view, anchor, 0, levels)`'s own rect, and the view is 3×3 chunks so the ring's growth exceeds the
lookahead's reach. 61/61 assertions pass; no starvation violation seen in any of the 60 rounds.

**Measured (lan5, `zoom_sweep_contract.py`'s canonical invocation — `--res 2560x1369 --water enhanced
--seconds 6`, 4090; `--res 1280x800`, Radeon iGPU, `ANNO_GPU_ADAPTER=1`), against 1c's own numbers (void
30-baseline set aside per the 1c review: pan compares against the unmodified-binary reruns, 100-127):**

| mode | 1c | 1c2 (the ring active) |
|---|---|---|
| legs | non-ready 35, stand-in 6032, dissolves 4533, open-sea 1544, >2ms 201 | non-ready 49, stand-in 9076, dissolves 4953, open-sea 1609, >2ms 202 |
| wheel | non-ready 31, stand-in 5332, dissolves 4618, open-sea 1462, >2ms 162 | non-ready 37, stand-in 5047, dissolves 4199, open-sea 1600, >2ms 157 |
| pan | non-ready 24-36, stand-in 0, dissolves 828-921, open-sea 1305-1398, >2ms 100-106 | non-ready 47, stand-in 0, dissolves 874, open-sea 1554, >2ms 113 |
| zoompan | non-ready 37, stand-in 14519, dissolves 6288, open-sea 1406, >2ms 189 | non-ready 50, stand-in 17002, dissolves 7799, open-sea 1711, >2ms 226 |
| iGPU wheel | non-ready 3, stand-in 0, dissolves 26, open-sea 44, >2ms 12 | non-ready 1-3 (3 runs), stand-in 0, dissolves 25-30, open-sea 45-54, >2ms 19-24 (3 runs) |

Pan's frames>2ms (113) is within 1c's own unmodified-binary comparison range (100-127), consistent with 1c's
finding that pan's busy tail on this machine is not a code-sensitive signal. The other three 4090 modes and
the iGPU's readiness counters (non-ready, stand-in, dissolves, open-sea) are all within run-to-run noise of
1c's own numbers — the ring does not starve anything, matching the step-4 test above. **The iGPU wheel's
busy-time tail is genuinely worse** (12 → 19-24 frames>2ms across three reruns, a consistent gap, not overlap):
readiness there (non-ready, dissolves, open-sea) tracks 1c closely, so this is not the readiness win costing
something elsewhere — it is the ring's own per-frame cost (computing `ring_view_at` and enumerating/sorting its
candidate chunks while zooming out) landing on a comparatively weak CPU/GPU pairing. Not fixed in this packet
(see Decisions).

off); that one file's `ANNO_EXTENSION_ORACLE_FILE` failure is the same pre-existing, unrelated gap already
present on `task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1`/`-1b`/`-1c` (a build-generated macro the standalone script does not set,
in `src/sim/tests`, nothing this packet touches). `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` flagged three lines across
`derived_freshness_test.cpp`; fixed in place (`-i`), rebuilt (`anno_render_tests`, `anno1503`, `bench_frame`),
reran the full render suite (212/212, unaffected) before measuring/gating.

NOT_RUN: the Radeon iGPU CTest gate (reasoned above, matching 1b/1c practice: no GPU-adapter code changed); WSL
ASan; `gpu.cpp`'s B2 prefetch gate and the GPU upload share (both out of scope, 1d's).

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Enlarged the step-9 test's view** (one chunk → 3×3 chunks) once the first attempt's `CHECK(saw_ring_key)`
  failure was traced to a real geometric fact, not a code bug: at the group-0/group-1 tile-width ratio this
  island actually has, a one-chunk view's ring never grows past the pan lookahead's own unconditional
  one-chunk border, so no view size that small could ever show ring-exclusive content, regardless of where the
  test looked for it. Fixing only the detection loop's group would have left the test unable to pass.
- **Reported the iGPU's worse busy-time tail rather than only the readiness-neutral result**, per the same
  packet-wide practice 1b and 1c already followed ("report better, equal or worse per level," not just the
  wins): the ring's own per-frame candidate-generation cost is a real, measured trade-off on the weaker
  adapter, distinct from the readiness counters (which did not regress), and is for a future packet (1d or a
  tuning pass) to weigh — e.g. capping the ring's candidate count, or skipping the ring once its target
  group's chunks are already fully resident — rather than something to patch under this packet's own time box
  without re-verifying the starvation invariant and the 4090 numbers again.
- **Left the ring at the *same* group as the view, not `group + 1` or a derived level**, per the dispatch's own
  wording ("the area a zoom-out to the coarse edge of the current level shows"): `zoomed_view_at` already
  covers the neighbouring-group case (rank 2), so the ring is deliberately a distinct, same-group concern.
- **Did not touch `gpu.cpp`'s prefetch gate (B2) or the upload share**, as instructed (both 1d's); nothing in
  steps 1-4 needed a change there — the ring's candidates flow through the same `ChunkKey` request path every
  other margin/adjacent candidate already uses.

QUESTIONs: is the iGPU wheel's +7 to +12 frames>2ms worth a follow-up tuning pass on its own (e.g. a per-frame
cap on ring candidates, or skipping the ring when the target group is already resident), or is it acceptable
as the Radeon's cost for the ring's readiness benefit on stronger hardware, left to a future general tuning
packet (1d, or after) to weigh against other candidates for the same budget of attention?

**READY FOR REVIEW.**

## ZOOM-SMOOTH-1d — the GPU upload share, B3 checked, the ring measured and turned off — READY FOR REVIEW (task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1d, from task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c2 `619f88f6`, head `63f4c69a`)

**B3, checked first, as asked.** The reaper (`ChunkWorkers::reap`, `frame.cpp`) runs at lowered thread priority;
the warm-plane pre-creation thread's own comment (`gpu.cpp`) already explains why that is unsafe for anything
touching the GPU: texture creation/destruction takes wgpu-hal's device allocator lock, which the window thread
also needs for every upload, so a lowered-priority thread holding it while descheduled is a real priority
inversion on the window thread - which is exactly why the warm-plane thread runs at normal priority instead.
**Confirmed: moving GPU resource releases onto the existing (CPU-side, lowered-priority) reaper would
reintroduce that same risk**, and this packet does not do that - step 5 below only widens *when* the existing
upload path runs, never moves any release onto a different thread. Checked wgpu-core's own resource-lifetime
tracking (wgpu-core 28.0.0/latest source, `device/life.rs`/`LifetimeTracker`; the exact v29.0.1.1 source wasn't
directly fetchable, so this is the closest confirmed version, not the pinned one): a resource's actual GPU-side
destruction is already deferred internally, by submission index, independently of when the caller releases it
- so Release/Destroy calls from any thread are correctness-safe regarding use-after-GPU-use; the risk is purely
the OS-level lock contention described above, not a wgpu-core lifetime bug. **Conclusion: B3's finding stands
as a reason never to route GPU releases through `reap()`, but does not block step 5, which doesn't do that.**

**Step 5: the GPU upload share.** Replaced the all-or-nothing prefetch gate (`!waiting && uploads == 0`, B2)
in `gpu.cpp sync_chunks`: prefetch (margin, adjacent, and - new - the ring) now also runs while a visible chunk
is waiting or one was already uploaded this frame, bounded by a new `GpuLimits::prefetch_budget_ms` (default
0.3 ms, a measured share - see below), spent in addition to `upload_budget_ms`, never out of it. Checked once
per prefetch candidate, so one multi-step `advance_upload` call already in flight may overrun the share
slightly (documented in the field's own comment); the next candidate is still stopped on time.

**Routed the ring into the GPU's prefetch for the first time.** Found while reading `plan_margin` for step 5:
the ring's rank-3 candidates (ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c2) were never added to `margin_`/`adjacent_` at all, so even with
B2 fixed, `gpu.cpp`'s prefetch loop (which only ever iterated those two lists) could never have uploaded a
ring chunk ahead - the dispatch's "it measured no readiness gain" is explained by this, not only by the gate.
Added `FrameRenderer::ring_keys()` (populated from rank-3 queue entries, same pattern as margin/adjacent),
threaded it through `sync_chunks`'s new `ring` parameter, and added it to the prefetch's list array, lowest
priority of the three (iterated last, so it never takes margin/adjacent's slot of `prefetch_chunks` within a
frame - margin and adjacent are always drained first).

**The ring switch:** `FrameRenderer::zoom_ring_enabled` (default **off**, see Decisions), `FrameConfig`'s own
field, `bench_frame --zoom-ring on|off`, and the viewer's `ANNO_VIEW_ZOOM_RING=on` debug env var (unset or any
other value leaves it off).

**Measured (lan5, bench_frame's zoom-sweep, 4090, 6 s/leg, same session, three runs per cell unless noted):**

| mode | ring off (= step 5 alone) | ring on (step 5 + ring) |
|---|---|---|
| legs | non-ready 47, stand-in 6801, dissolves 5034, open-sea 1691, >2ms 216 | non-ready 47, stand-in 7076, dissolves 4994, open-sea 1472, >2ms 219 |
| wheel | non-ready 35, stand-in 6011, dissolves 4600, open-sea 1625, >2ms 164 | non-ready 35, stand-in 4501, dissolves 3928, open-sea 1504, >2ms 161 |
| pan | non-ready 43, stand-in 0, dissolves 1002, open-sea 1688, >2ms 94 | non-ready 41, stand-in 0, dissolves 808, open-sea 1431, >2ms 105 |
| zoompan (3 runs) | stand-in 14489-15847, dissolves 6706-7116, open-sea 1665-1694, >2ms 173-210 | stand-in 20390-23549, dissolves 9491-10778, open-sea 1922-2136, >2ms 221-250 |
| iGPU wheel (3 runs each; see Decisions on the baseline) | >2ms 18-41 | >2ms 23-42 |

**Against 1c2's own numbers** (step 5 absent, old gate, ring generated on the CPU but never reaching the GPU):
legs 202/9076(stand-in)→**ring-off 216/6801**; wheel 157/5047→**164/6011**; pan 113/0→**94/0**; zoompan
226/17002→**173/14489**. So **step 5 alone is a clear win on every mode**, zoompan most of all (open-sea
1711→1688, dissolves 7799→7116, >2ms 226→173-210).

**The ring, once actually routed to the GPU, does not add a net win on top of step 5.** Wheel and pan move a
little further in the right direction with it on; **zoompan gets consistently, repeatably worse** (three runs
each side, non-overlapping: stand-in about 21.9k vs 14.9k, dissolves about 10.1k vs 7.0k, >2ms about 237 vs
197). Both share the same `GpuLimits::prefetch_chunks`/`prefetch_budget_ms` budget, lowest priority to the
ring within it - but zoompan is exactly the mode under the most pressure on that shared budget already, so
giving the ring a slice of it (even a strictly lower-priority one) measurably costs the mode that needed it
most. Per the dispatch's own rule ("if it helps on the 4090 but costs the iGPU, that trade isn't yours to
make" - here the cost is on the 4090 itself, in the worst mode, which the rule's spirit covers just as much):
**turned the ring off by default**, kept as code and a switch (not deleted) for a future packet that gives it
its own, separate budget instead of sharing margin/adjacent's.

**The iGPU wheel numbers needed their own baseline check first.** The dispatch's own 1c2 review number (12
frames>2ms) turned out to be **void, the same way 1c found pan's 30-baseline void**: rerunning the completely
unmodified `task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1c2` binary, right now, three times, gives 14/18/21 - matching 1c2's *own*
recorded range (19-24), not 1c's 12. Every 1d configuration tested (ring on, ring off, and step 5 fully
disabled via the new `--prefetch-budget-ms 0`) gives 18-42 across runs, overlapping that unmodified-binary
range; nothing here points to a real 1d-caused iGPU regression, only the same day-to-day iGPU variance 1c
already documented for pan. **Compare future iGPU wheel numbers against 14-24, not against 12.**

**Added `--prefetch-budget-ms n`** (bench_frame, mirrors `--prefetch`/`--chunk-budget-mb`): overrides
`GpuLimits::prefetch_budget_ms`, used here to isolate step 5's own gate change from the ring for the iGPU
baseline check above; kept as a permanent diagnostic, same reasoning as `--resident-prewarm`.

**Gates.** MSVC Release, game files, render+app: `COUNTS: selected=496 executed=493 failed=0 empty=0
skipped=3 (opt-in=3) incomplete=0 sanitizer_lines=0` / `VERDICT: PASS`
(`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1d-render-app-1.log`). GPU, 4090: `COUNTS: selected=117 executed=117 failed=0 empty=0
skipped=0 incomplete=0 sanitizer_lines=0` / `VERDICT: PASS` (`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1d-gpu-4090.log`). The
Radeon iGPU CTest gate was not rerun (no GPU-adapter correctness code changed; only `GpuLimits` fields and the
prefetch/upload-ahead policy, exercised above). WSL `-Werror` check: clean except the same pre-existing,
unrelated `src/sim/tests/extensions_test.cpp` gap. `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` flagged 7 lines across
`gpu.cpp`/`viewer.cpp`; fixed in place, rebuilt (`anno_render_tests`/`anno1503`/`bench_frame`/
`anno_render_gpu_tests`/`anno_app_tests`), reran the full render suite (212/212, including the ring's own
starvation test re-enabled explicitly for itself) and the GPU/app suites (117/117, 284/284) - all unaffected.

NOT_RUN: **the packet's own full target** (0 on all four counters for zoom-out moves and returns, centre and
off centre, via the live owner-style session - `zoom-session-2026-11-14/zoom.script` +
`tools/drive2.py`/`analyze2.py`) - this packet's time went to B3, step 5's design and the ring's measurement
(which turned up the "never reached the GPU at all" finding and the zoompan regression, neither anticipated
by the dispatch), leaving no safe remaining time to also stand up and analyse a live capture session without
rushing it; zoom-in (reported only, per the packet); the Radeon iGPU CTest gate (reasoned above); WSL ASan;
`gpu.cpp`'s B2 gate change beyond this packet's own fix (none further needed); the GPU upload share's own
separate budget for the ring (deferred to whichever future packet revisits it).

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Turned the ring off by default rather than deleting it.** The geometry (`ring_view_at`), the
  zoom-direction signal and the starvation-invariant test are all independently correct (1c2's review
  confirmed this, and nothing here changes it); the measured problem is specifically that it shares
  `prefetch_chunks`/`prefetch_budget_ms` with margin/adjacent, not that the ring's own logic is wrong. Keeping
  the code and the switch costs nothing and lets a future packet try giving it a separate share instead of
  re-deriving the geometry from scratch.
- **Checked whether the iGPU numbers were drift before trusting them**, the same discipline 1c used for pan:
  before concluding 1d regressed the iGPU, reran the *unmodified* 1c2 binary and found it does not reproduce
  its own review's quoted 12 either - the right comparison is 1c2's own range, which nothing in 1d moved.
  Reporting an invented iGPU regression from 1d, when the unmodified prior code already shows the same
  numbers today, would have been the kind of unevidenced claim the project's evidence contract rules out.
- **Stopped before the live-session proof** rather than rushing it in whatever time was left: the dispatch's
  own escape clause ("if it outgrows the box, stop and report what's done") and the evidence contract's
  "known failures remain failures" both argue for reporting this honestly as NOT_RUN over presenting a
  skimmed or unverified pass at the packet's hardest proof item.
- **Added `--prefetch-budget-ms`** as a permanent diagnostic (not reverted after use) for the same reason
  `--resident-prewarm` was kept in 1c: isolating one knob at a time is how the iGPU drift question got settled
  here, and it will be needed again whenever the ring's own separate budget is designed.

QUESTIONs: does a future packet give the ring its own, separate slice of `prefetch_chunks`/
`prefetch_budget_ms` (so it stops competing with margin/adjacent on zoompan) rather than sharing theirs, and
is that worth doing before or after the live-session proof (NOT_RUN here) actually measures whether 0-on-all-
four-counters is reachable without the ring at all, now that step 5 alone has moved every mode a long way
there?

**READY FOR REVIEW.**

## ZOOM-SMOOTH-1e — F1, F2, the live proof measured and NOT MET — READY FOR REVIEW (task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1e, from task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-1d `1f7a5a9f`, head `84e6fc53`)

**F1 (the step-5 test).** New GPU test, `gpu_test.cpp`: a two-chunk view with `uploads_per_frame = 1` leaves
one visible chunk real and one still waiting within a single render call (deterministic regardless of how
trivially fast the scene's own content uploads - an earlier attempt using "never insert the view's own chunk"
failed because an empty scene uploads it instantly anyway). With a margin chunk inserted and
`prefetch_budget_ms = 0`, `chunks_prefetched == 0` (the pre-1d gate's exact behaviour); with `> 0`,
`chunks_prefetched == 1` although the visible chunk still waits. Deliberately not `test_hold_uploads`: the
prefetch block's own gate also checks `!test_hold_uploads`, which would close prefetch too and defeat the
test. Fails on `619f88f6`: `GpuLimits::prefetch_budget_ms` does not exist on that commit at all.

**F2 (the citation).** `docs/perf/README.md` ZOOM-SMOOTH-1d's own section: what the gate replaces, the exact
field and default (0.3 ms), why that figure (a reasoned starting share, verified by measurement, not
asserted), the full before/after table against 1c2 already in REPORTS, and the `--prefetch-budget-ms`
isolation flag used to settle the iGPU baseline-drift question.

**The live owner-style proof (zoom.script / drive2.py / analyze2.py), ring off (the default), 4090, lan5,
enhanced water, 5 locations (north, middle, sea, southeast, west) x 6 modes (osc, fullout, fullin, flick,
human, panzoom).** Added `wheel N X Y` to `dev_script.cpp` (arity -1, like `click_px`'s nullable x/y) for the
off-centre half the original task spec always deferred - a parse+exec test (`dev_script_test.cpp`,
`anno_app_input_tests`) confirms `wheel N` stays centred and `wheel N X Y` lands at the raw position, and that
exactly 2 arguments fails to step (not a valid count). Off-centre position: `(1920, 890)`, the project's own
25%/15% off-centre-anchor convention (`bench_frame`'s `s.anchor_x = 0.25 * w; s.anchor_y = 0.15 * h;`) applied
as an absolute pixel offset from the window's centre on its established 2560x1369 client size.

**The target is NOT MET.** Dissolves are nonzero in *every* osc phase at both positions, and in several
fullout phases too; several locations also show nonzero non-ready frames (missing content actually visible,
not just a dissolve's tail):

| phase | centre: non-ready/frames (most) | centre: dissolves (most) | off-centre: non-ready/frames (most) | off-centre: dissolves (most) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| north-osc | 0/1974 | 98 (10) | 0/1991 | 119 (13) |
| north-fullout | 0/997 | 7 (5) | 0/0 | 0 |
| middle-osc | 7/982 (7) | 77 (7) | 24/980 (5) | 157 (8) |
| sea-osc | 0/1992 | 79 (11) | 0/1993 | 25 (4) |
| sea-fullout | 0/1000 | 208 (10) | 0/999 | 204 (13) |
| southeast-osc | 18/1989 (2) | 80 (6) | 79/989 (14) | 163 (10) |
| southeast-fullin | 0/1000 | 0 | 35/996 (19) | 34 (27) |
| west-osc | 16/1988 (5) | 90 (2) | 66/1983 (15) | 148 (11) |
| west-fullin-end | 0/1001 | 0 | 47/986 (6) | 172 (25) |

Every one of the 5 locations' `-osc` phases has nonzero dissolves at both positions (the full per-phase tables,
all 5 locations x 6 modes x 2 positions, are in `cache/`'s `run-1e-centre/analysis.txt` and
`run-1e-offcentre/analysis.txt`, not checked in - original-rendered content). Off-centre is consistently worse
or equal, never better: southeast's osc goes from 18/1989 non-ready, 80 dissolves (centre) to 79/989, 163
(off-centre) - more than quadruple the non-ready rate.

**The fourth and fifth counters, stand-in draws and open-sea ("late island") draws, were not separately
instrumented by this proof.** The viewer's own `--play` report line (what `drive2.py`'s trace captures) prints
only "not ready" and "dissolved chunks"; `bench_frame`'s synthetic sweep is the only harness that reports
stand-in/open-sea separately (1b/1c/1c2/1d's own measurements). A stand-in draw and an open-sea draw are each a
*sub-classification* of a non-ready frame (a frame is counted as non-ready, then drawn as either a stand-in or
open sea, never both) - so where non-ready is 0, both are structurally 0 too (north-fullout, sea-fullout, and
most non-"-osc" phases above). Where non-ready is **not** 0 (middle/southeast/west-osc at both positions,
southeast-fullin and west-fullin-end off-centre), this proof cannot say how those non-ready frames split
between stand-in and open-sea - but the target already fails on non-ready and dissolves alone in those phases,
so this gap does not change the bottom line.

**Gates.** MSVC Release, game files, render+app+GPU+input combined: `COUNTS: selected=651 executed=648
failed=0 empty=0 skipped=3 (opt-in=3) incomplete=0 sanitizer_lines=0` / `VERDICT: PASS`
(`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1e-render-app-1.log`) - clean, no refusals. GPU, 4090, separately:
`COUNTS: selected=118 executed=118 failed=0 empty=0 skipped=0 incomplete=0 sanitizer_lines=0` / `VERDICT:
PASS` (`cache/gates/zoomsmooth1e-gpu-4090.log`). `anno_render_gpu_tests` 118/118 (117 + F1's new case);
`anno_app_tests` 284/284; `anno_app_input_tests` 37/37 (both unaffected by the `wheel` change beyond its own
new test). WSL `-Werror` check: clean except the same pre-existing, unrelated `extensions_test.cpp` gap.
`clang-format --dry-run --Werror` flagged 2 lines in `dev_script_test.cpp`; fixed in place, rebuilt
(`anno_render_gpu_tests`/`anno_app_input_tests`/`anno_app_tests`/`anno1503`), reran all three suites
unaffected before gating.

NOT_RUN: tuning any of the live-proof findings above - explicitly out of scope per the dispatch ("do not
tune"). The ring's own separate prefetch budget (QUESTION from 1d, now answered: not needed first, since step
5 alone does not reach 0 either - see Decisions). WSL ASan. A full off-centre/centre matrix beyond the 5
locations x 6 modes already run (none - this packet's own scope was exactly that matrix, now complete).

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Stopped at the first clear failure rather than tuning**, per the dispatch's own instruction. The dissolve
  counter alone, nonzero in every single osc phase across 5 locations and 2 positions with no exception,
  is sufficient evidence that 0-on-all-counters is not reached by step 5 alone (ring off); continuing to
  measure more scenarios would not have changed that conclusion, and attempting a fix was explicitly
  out of scope for this packet.
- **Chose off-centre = (1920, 890)** from the project's own existing 25%/15% convention (`bench_frame`'s
  `anchor_x`/`anchor_y`) rather than an arbitrary pixel, applied to the established 2560x1369 window size this
  exact host's prior zoom sessions have consistently reported, so the off-centre run is comparable to earlier
  off-centre measurements elsewhere in the project (e.g. `adjacent_keys`'s own anchor tests) rather than an
  unrelated one-off choice.
- **Used `uploads_per_frame = 1` over `test_hold_uploads` for F1**, after the first attempt (assuming an
  unbuilt chunk would stay unbuilt) failed because the empty test scene uploads trivially fast regardless of
  workers - `test_hold_uploads` was ruled out because the prefetch gate itself checks it, which would have
  closed prefetch too and made the test vacuous.
- **Reasoned, rather than measured, that stand-in/open-sea are implied 0 where non-ready is 0**, since the
  viewer's own instrumentation does not print them separately and adding that instrumentation was outside this
  packet's "touch nothing else." Stated the gap honestly for the phases where non-ready is not 0, rather than
  assuming those two counters are fine there too.

QUESTIONs: given step 5 alone (ring off) does not reach 0 either, is the next step a different fix inside
`gpu.cpp`'s upload-ahead (e.g. a bigger prefetch share, or routing it earlier in the frame), a return to the
ring with its own separate budget, or does this call for RENDER-DIRECT's removal of stand-ins/dissolves
altogether rather than continuing to chase 0 inside the current chunk-renderer's architecture? Is the
dissolve pattern's near-universality (every single osc phase, both positions, all 5 locations) itself evidence
that `chunk_fade_ms` (150 ms) is inherent to *any* zoom-out-and-return under the current chunk model, not a
tunable bug?

**READY FOR REVIEW.**
