## ZOOM-SMOOTH-3b: classify the finish spikes — draws correlate with `finish` where measured; the
original 4.4-10.8 ms spikes were not reproduced this time; two concrete, evidenced background-
thread candidates named for next — READY FOR REVIEW (task/ZOOM-SMOOTH-3, same worktree and branch,
on top of `953ca181`/`3526d253`)

**Items 1-2 (`GpuStats`, `gpu.hpp`/`gpu.cpp`): the counts review F1/F2 asked for.** `chunks_visible`
(`visible_chunks(view).size()`, already computed at the `sync_chunks` call and now just kept) is the
real per-frame drawn count; the hitch line now prints "chunks built N, missing N, drawn N" instead
of the old, mislabelled "visible chunks" (`chunks_built + chunks_missing`, which review F1 correctly
called 0-at-rest and not what the name said). `draw_calls`/`bind_group_sets` are counted at every
`wgpuRenderPassEncoderDraw`/`SetBindGroup` call inside `GpuFrame::render` (the per-chunk `draw_chunks`
lambda - the dominant, content-scaling source across the terrain/ground/sea/objects/sea-over passes
- plus the sprite, resample and UI-overlay passes); the one `SetBindGroup(p, 0, pass1/pass2, ...)` per
render pass (3 a frame, fixed) is left out as noise, documented in the field's own comment.

**Item 3 (CPU vs wall time of `finish`): the chosen API turned out too coarse to answer this.**
`thread_priority.hpp` gained `thread_cpu_time_ms()` (`GetThreadTimes` on Windows, kernel+user ticks to
ms; `clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)` elsewhere), bracketed around the same
`wgpuCommandEncoderFinish` call `SubmitTimes::finish` already times, as `finish_cpu_ms`. Measured: on
this machine `GetThreadTimes` only updates in ~15.6 ms system-clock-quantum steps - every nonzero
sample read exactly **15.62 ms**, regardless of whether the matching `finish_ms` was 0.57, 0.85, 1.05
or 1.78 ms (`live_run/stderr.log`, e.g. t=3.09-3.25s), and it read 0 on the rest (3655/3673 live,
3688/3728 control frames). The code is correct and wired through to the hitch line and `FrameCounts`,
but it cannot distinguish "computing" from "waiting" at a sub-quantum scale, and the original 4-10 ms
spikes are themselves below one quantum - **inconclusive by this method, not negative evidence of
either**. `QueryThreadCycleTime` (TSC cycles) would need the core's actual clock frequency to convert
to time, which has no reliable API; a more direct test would log the background threads' own
create/release timestamps (item 6) against window-thread spike timestamps instead of sampling CPU
time at all - left for whoever next measures an actual spike directly.

**Item 4 (8-frame look-back): implemented, wired to the hitch line, not yet exercised on a real
spike.** `counts_history_` (a `std::deque<FrameCounts>`, `kLookback` = 8) is updated after each hitch
check, so it holds the frames strictly before the one just measured. When the current frame's own
`finish_ms` exceeds `kSlowFinishMs` = 2.0 (ZOOM-MEASURE-1's own control-sweep line, review F4), the
hitch line gets a second row: summed `planes_freed`/`chunks_dropped`/`sprites_decoded` over the
look-back. No slow finish occurred in either measurement run (next item), so this has not yet been
checked against a real spike - the mechanism is in place and will print the next time one happens
under a hitch-tracing run.

**Item 5 (distribution, live + control): measured, but did not reproduce the original spike
magnitude.** Two `drive2.py` sessions (max zoom-out, `wheel -60`; live = six pan/wheel gestures over
~5 s, control = camera at rest for 8 s; `ANNO_VIEW_HITCH_MS=0` so every frame logs, not just hitches;
3,673 and 3,728 frames) parsed for `finish_ms`/`draw_calls`:
- live: median 0.320 ms, p99 1.156 ms, p99.9 1.906 ms, **max 2.320 ms**; 3 frames over 2 ms.
- control: median 0.460 ms, p99 1.190 ms, p99.9 1.635 ms, **max 1.720 ms**; 0 frames over 2 ms.
- Both match ZOOM-MEASURE-1's own control figure (2/1,980 over 2 ms, max 3.11 ms) order of magnitude
  for order; **neither run came close to the 4.4-10.8 ms spikes ZOOM-SMOOTH-3 found** - that session's
  scenario (likely a heavier draw/upload load, or a cold-cache transient this 5-8 s script did not
  hit) was not reproduced here, so the correlation below is evidence about `finish`'s normal range,
  not a direct measurement of the worst-case spikes themselves. **QUESTION, not a guess.**
- `corr(draw_calls, finish_ms)` over all frames: **0.85 (live), 0.77 (control)** - `draw_calls` ranged
  109-689 across frames at this zoom level. This is real, not assumed: ZOOM-SMOOTH-3's own gap (F2,
  not tracking the one count that tests its own hypothesis) is closed, and the hypothesis holds over
  the range measured.

**Item 6 (non-window-thread wgpu callers; read-only, no change).**
- `gpu.cpp`, `Impl::start_prewarm()`'s `warm_thread` lambda (lines ~549-607): calls `make_texture`/
  `make_view` (`wgpuDeviceCreateTexture`/`wgpuTextureCreateView`) to pre-build "warm" chunk planes.
  The surrounding comment already says why this matters: texture creation takes wgpu-hal's device
  allocator lock, the same lock every window-thread upload and buffer creation needs.
- `gpu_fluid.cpp`, `FluidGpu::prepare_window()`'s job `thread` (lines ~733-747), via `make_grid()`
  (lines ~243-285): calls `grid_texture()` (`wgpuDeviceCreateTexture`/`wgpuTextureCreateView`) and
  `wgpuDeviceCreateBindGroup` directly, building a whole new fluid-simulation grid off the window
  thread.
- `gpu_fluid.cpp`, `FluidGpu::free_job_in_background()` (lines ~639-650): its own detached thread's
  `j.reset()` destructs a retired `Job`, including an unapplied `Grid` if one was built before
  cancellation (`make_grid` runs to completion regardless of `cancel`, only `compute_pieces`'s loop
  checks it) - this **releases** that grid's `Texture`/`TextureView`/`BindGroup` handles
  (`Handle<..., wgpuTextureRelease>` etc., `wgpu.hpp`) off the window thread. This is the one
  genuine background-thread wgpu *release* found, matching the task's own "releases" category.
- Checked and ruled out: `frame.cpp`'s chunk-builder thread pool and `reaper_` thread (CPU pixel
  compositing and CPU chunk freeing only, no `wgpu` symbol in the file); `scene.cpp`'s
  `SceneReclaimer` thread (`delete`s CPU-only `Scene` generations - `Scene` owns no `Texture`/`Plane`
  members, confirmed by reading `scene.hpp`).

**Conclusion (one, with evidence; marked where it is a guess).** Over the range this measurement
could reach (0.1-2.3 ms), `finish_ms` tracks `draw_calls` closely (r = 0.77-0.85) - **computing**, not
waiting, is the dominant story there, confirming the task's own hypothesis directly instead of by
elimination. For the original 4.4-10.8 ms spikes specifically, this packet has **no direct
measurement** (not reproduced) and the CPU-time instrumentation (item 3) cannot resolve sub-quantum
waits either way - so "waiting on a lock, descheduled, or paying for another thread's deferred wgpu
work" is **not confirmed, not ruled out**. **Guess, not evidence:** item 6's two background-thread
candidates (the plane pre-creation thread's own texture/view creation, and the fluid job's grid
creation/release) are the most concrete things found that could make the window thread's own
`wgpuCommandEncoderFinish` wait on wgpu-hal's shared device allocator lock - they are named because
they are the only background wgpu callers that exist, not because either was caught in the act of a
spike.

**No fix made** (task's own instruction: measurement and diagnostics only).

**Gates (changed lanes: app, render/render-gpu for the `GpuStats` fields).** `anno_app_tests`,
`anno_render_tests`, `anno_render_gpu_tests`: 615/615 after a solo rerun of 8 tests that first failed
only under memory contention from the concurrent `drive2.py` capture sessions (unrelated to this
diff - chunk-draw/river-digest/river-flow corpus tests; none of them touch `viewer.cpp`, `gpu.hpp`,
`gpu.cpp` or `thread_priority.hpp`), matching the project's own "refused tests rerun alone"

**The spikes were reproduced this time (F1).** Two full five-location sessions (`north`, `middle`,

  0 over 4 ms.

Two runs already had a call over 4 ms (combined), so per the task's own stop rule this did not need the
two further runs.

(stable across the whole session - the CPU's own clock, confirmed not drifting meaningfully run to run).

`prewarm_begin_ns`/`end_ns` (the plane pre-creation thread's own texture/view build),

**The 29 slow calls found (26 + 2 + 1 counted once; 27 printed detail lines in run 1, 2 in run 2), every

  pre-creation thread and the fluid job's build/release are not implicated for *these* spikes, by direct

  band matches ZOOM-MEASURE-1's own control-sweep figure (2/1,980 frames over 2 ms, max 3.11 ms) in

  run 2's) show tens of planes freed and chunks dropped in the 8 frames before them. No single look-back

overlap with either known background section) are **descheduled** - not computing (the cycle count rules

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Fed the yardstick on every ordinary frame, not only frames that print a hitch** - the first version of
  this logic lived inside the `if (gap > hitch_ms())` block and would have almost never fed it (an ordinary

  most of which were already applied (no grid left to release); logging every one of those as a "release"

- **`build_begin_ns_`/`build_end_ns_`/`release_begin_ns_`/`release_end_ns_` are `shared_ptr<atomic<int64_t>>`,

  `free_job_in_background`'s detached thread hold its own reference, independent of this object's lifetime,
  the same reason `freeing_` itself already uses one.
- **Stopped at two runs**, per the task's own rule, once both runs' combined 4 ms+ count was nonzero (2),
  rather than running two more to no new information.

## ZOOM-BOUNCE-2 — not reproduced hammering both limits; the clamp regression-tested — READY FOR REVIEW (same branch task/ZOOM-BOUNCE-1, new commits, no rebase)

**The hypothesis refuted, so checked the leads directly rather than assume more.** Extended
`ANNO_VIEW_TRACE`'s own `frames.tsv` with three new columns (`resample_scale`, `resample_offset_x/y`: the
`gpu::Resample` actually handed to `FrameRenderer::render`, captured at the same point `scale` already is) -
lead 3's own ask, "the scale that is presented, not only the view state," for free from existing
infrastructure. `tools/bench/window_table.py`'s `COLUMNS` and its contract test updated to match (columns
appended at the end, not inserted, so none of that test's many positional `sed` edits needed touching).

**The script** (`tools/test/viewer_wiring/zoom_bounce_2.script`, same cursor and window size): drives hard
to each zoom limit, then sends several more notches in the same direction with as little gap as the script
can express (0 ms and 3 ms, some back to back with no wait at all - lead 1's "within a few frames of each
other"), alternating the closest and farthest limit, 40 repeats = 960 wheel events, **21,775 presented
frames**. Confirmed the closest limit was genuinely reached and hammered, not approximated: the recorded
`resample_scale * tile_w(group)` peaked at 118.79364, against the exact theoretical limit
`84 * sqrt(2) = 118.79394` - matched to four decimals, repeatedly, with the extra inward notches still
landing on top of it.

**Checked, all clean:**
- `scale` (view state) vs `resample_scale` (presented): **0 mismatches** over 0.05 %, across all 21,775
  frames - rules out lead 3 directly; `resampled_view`'s own grid-fit clamp (`resample.cpp`) is confirmed a
  no-op in this scale range (`fit ≈ 0.315` for this window size, far below any scale near a zoom limit), so
  it was never going to diverge here, but this is now measured, not assumed.
- A one-frame spike in the presented, group-independent eased tile width against smooth neighbours (the
  owner's own signature: one frame far from both its neighbours, which agree with each other): **0 spikes**.
- A group that flips for one frame and reverts: **0 flickers** (unchanged from ZOOM-BOUNCE-1).
- `drawable_w`/`drawable_h` (the window's own reported size): **rock steady at 2560 x 1369 on every single
  frame** of the whole run - rules out a window-size blip producing the same "whole view scaled" look lead 2
  raised as a possibility.

**Lead 1 is also false by construction, not just by measurement.** `zoom_target_after`'s clamp
(`std::clamp(target * factor, lowest, levels.tile_w(0) * kZoomEndFactor)`) is applied on every single call,
inside the one function `zoom_by` ever calls - there is no intermediate state in which an unclamped value
exists for even one frame, with or without an intervening `zoom_advance`. Proved this directly: a new test
(below) calls it 20 times in a row from exactly at the limit, with no advance between calls (exactly what
several same-frame wheel events would produce) - the target never moves, let alone past the limit, by even
a floating-point hair.

**Added a permanent regression test** (`app_test.cpp`): `zoom_target_after` from exactly at the closest-zoom
limit, 20 repeated inward notches with no `zoom_advance` between them, asserting the target stays exactly
at the limit every time (`<=`, not just `Approx`) - proves lead 1's own mechanism cannot occur in this code,
not just that this run didn't show it.

**Did not reproduce.** No fix made - nothing to fix at the cause the leads named. `view_w`/`view_h`/`group`/
`scale`/`resample_scale`/`resample_offset_x/y`/`drawable_w`/`drawable_h` were all checked and all clean,
hammering the exact scenario (reaching a true limit, extra same-direction notches arriving with no gap) the
owner's own session plausibly produced. What remains unchecked is everything inside `FrameRenderer::render`'s
own per-layer compositing (`frame.cpp`/`gpu.cpp`) and the capture itself - the same two items ZOOM-BOUNCE-1's
own entry named, still open.

**Gates (changed lanes only, per the instruction).** `anno_app_tests`: 284/284
(`cache/gates/zoombounce2-app-1.log`). `viewer_wiring_contract` + `window_tools_contract`: 2/2
(`cache/gates/zoombounce2-viewerwiringcontract-1.log`). `window_table_contract` (the Python reader's own
contract test) only registers on UNIX (`CMakeLists.txt`: `if(ANNO_BUILD_TESTS AND UNIX)`), so it never runs
on this Windows gate; verified the two `sed` substitutions my column change touched by hand against the new
header/rows (both produce the expected row), and hosted Linux CI is the real check for it. WSL `-Werror`:
clean on every file this packet touched, same pre-existing `extensions_test.cpp` gap as every other packet
this cycle. `clang-format` clean.

NOT_RUN: `FrameRenderer`/`gpu.cpp`-internal instrumentation (still the open item from ZOOM-BOUNCE-1); a
capture-side check of the owner's own recording; the render suite (not run - this packet changes no render
code, per the instruction not to run it for an unrelated lane).

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Extended the existing `ANNO_VIEW_TRACE` facility rather than adding a second, parallel trace mechanism**
  for "the scale handed to the renderer" - `resample` is already a parameter at the exact call site `scale`
  is read, so this needed one new read, not new plumbing.
- **Appended the new columns instead of inserting them**, once the contract test's own dozens of
  position-sensitive `sed` substitutions made clear that an insertion would need touching most of them for
  no benefit - the column's own name, not its position, is what every reader keys on.

  assuming 10-14 notches of magnitude 12 would obviously clear it - the recorded value matched the closed

- **Proved lead 1 false by construction, not only by absence of evidence in one run** - a clamp applied

## ZOOM-BOUNCE-3 — the bounce hypothesis reproduces almost exactly — READY FOR REVIEW (same branch task/ZOOM-BOUNCE-1, new commits, no rebase)

**Traced every wheel event into the existing window trace** (`wheel.tsv`, recorded whenever
`ANNO_VIEW_TRACE` is already running - no new switch): `t_ms`, the raw float and accumulated-
integer deltas SDL gives (`SDL_MouseWheelEvent::y`/`integer_y`), the flipped flag, the pointer
position, and `zoom_target_` just before and after that one event's own `zoom_by()` call.

**The scripted pair** (`zoom_bounce_3.script`): one inward tick, then one outward tick 5, 10 and
20 ms later, at rest between 20 and 42 tile width (away from either limit). Read `wheel.tsv`
against `frames.tsv`'s own `resample_scale` (same clock) frame by frame:

| gap | peak scale reached | excursion over the 20/42 rest value | frames it shows in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 ms | 0.4832 | **+1.47 %** | 1 (the very next drawn frame; already reversing the one after) |
| 10 ms | 0.4876 | **+2.40 %** | 2 |
| 20 ms | 0.4956 | **+4.08 %** | 3-4 |

**The 5 ms result is the owner's own number, to within measurement precision**: the reported
frame was "the whole view zoomed in by about 1.5 %" - this packet's own 5 ms pair peaks at
**1.47 %**, one frame after the inward tick, reversing by the very next one. The excursion grows
roughly linearly with the gap (consistent with the easing's own early-time behaviour, first-order
in `dt`), so a brief double-tick anywhere under about 10 ms plausibly explains a single captured
frame differing by 1-2 %, exactly as reported - without any readiness miss, group flicker or
presented/view-state disagreement, all of which ZOOM-BOUNCE-1/2 already ruled out.

**No zoom change.** This is a finding about the input, not the easing or the renderer: the target
correctly reflects every tick it receives, including a brief reversal, and the view correctly
eases toward whatever the latest target is. Whether a double-tick this close together is ever
really intended by the user, and so whether it is worth filtering, is the owner's own call - a feel
change, per the instruction.

**The owner's recipe.** With `ANNO_VIEW_LIVE_RESIZE_TRACE` unrelated, just the usual:
```powershell
$env:ANNO_VIEW_TRACE = "wheel-trace-1"
.\build\msvc\src\app\Release\anno1503.exe --play data\maps\lan5.txt --game-dir E:\anno1503\game\app --water enhanced
```
Wheel in and out quickly, varying speed, for about 20 s, then close the window. In
`wheel-trace-1\trace\wheel.tsv`, sort by `t_ms` and flag any two consecutive rows whose `raw_y`
signs differ with `t_ms` less than 30 ms apart - that count, and how often it happens during an
ordinary fast scroll, is what decides whether this is rare or constant.

**Gates (changed lane: app).** `anno_app_tests` + `viewer_wiring_*`: 307/307
(`cache/gates/zoombounce3-app-1.log`). WSL `-Werror`: clean on every file this packet touched,
same pre-existing `extensions_test.cpp` gap. `clang-format` clean after one `-i` fix.

NOT_RUN: the owner's own 20 s recipe (above, not yet run); whether a double-tick this close
together occurs during the owner's own ordinary play (not measured here - only the scripted pair).

Decisions and reasoning:
- **Reused the existing `ANNO_VIEW_TRACE` switch rather than adding a new one**, since the window
  trace is already off by default; a second toggle would only add a step the owner has to remember.
- **Read `wheel.tsv` against `frames.tsv`'s own clock, not a new correlation mechanism** - both
  already share `WindowTrace::now_ms()`/`ms_at()`, so no new plumbing was needed to line them up.
- **Reported the exact matching number (1.47 % against the owner's 1.5 %) rather than just "yes, a
  bounce can cause an excursion"** - the close match is what makes this a strong finding, not a
  plausible-sounding one.
- **Did not add a filter or a minimum-gap guard**, per the instruction - a scroll-wheel feel change
  is the owner's decision, not a fix this packet should make unasked.

QUESTIONs: does the owner's own hardware (recipe above) actually produce opposite-sign ticks under
30 ms apart during ordinary fast scrolling, and if so, is filtering them wanted as a feel change?

READY FOR REVIEW.

## RENDER-DIRECT-1a — resident sprite atlases measured, layout fixed — READY FOR REVIEW (task/RENDER-DIRECT-1a, new worktree from `origin/main` `ac02d4a2`)

**Command.** `bench_frame <game_dir> <file> --atlas-report out.tsv [--atlas-gpu-limits]` (a mode of
`bench_frame`, not a second tool/implementation: reuses `load_any_scene`, `prepare_objects`,
`animation`/`frame_index`, `AtlasResidency` directly). `<file>` "-" walks the whole corpus
(`<game_dir>/Scenes` recursive + `data/maps/lan5.txt` + the 3 `ship-start-v2` candidates); any
other `<file>` measures just that one scene. Full doc: `docs/render/atlas.md`.

**Run.** 519 scenes (515 `.sze`/`.scp`, `lan5.txt`, 3 candidates), native MSVC, 0 refused, 7m12s
wall. Worst case across every page/padding/mip combo: `01_1024_easy_256.sze` group 0, 268,435,456
bytes (exactly 256 MiB — one of two combos hitting that number, named explicitly rather than used
as "the" worst-case figure, since it is a round page count, not a tight measured need). Under the
**recommended layout** (2048 px page, 2 px padding, no mips) the group-0 worst is a different
scene, `02_1024_easy_128.sze`: 218,103,808 bytes (208 MiB), **48 MiB headroom inside the 256 MiB
iGPU budget** (304 MiB headroom on the 4090's 512 MiB). Median (same layout, 1,557 scene×group
rows): 16,777,216 bytes (16 MiB, one page). `lan5.txt` group 0: 117,440,512 bytes (7 pages).

**Figures (whole FigurenHeader.dat, once):** group 0, 241,808 frames / 1,923.4 MiB — matches
`sprite_fidelity_test.cpp`'s own oracle count exactly, a direct cross-check. Too large to keep
resident (ADR 0007's own premise); `scene.units` (`load_scene` only, not `load_placed_scene` —
`lan5.txt`/candidates report 0 for this reason, not because they have none) gives the few hundred
KB to a few MB a scene actually needs, via `render::FrameKey::unit`, the frame table's own
identity.

**Player colours.** Static (Anlagen.dat): `SpriteCache::get`/`assets::building::to_rgba` have no
colour parameter at all, and `player_coloured`/`recolour` are called only from
`assets/src/unit.cpp` — 0 static frames are ever recoloured today, structurally, not by
inspection of intent. Decoded anyway (not assumed): of 27,537 non-shadow Anlagen frames, **11,180
(40.6 %) have at least one pixel** the decoder's own green-dominance test would match — 3,760,786
of 102,530,209 pixels (3.67 %) — a real finding about the files, separate from the engine's
current behaviour. Figures: 35,423 of 241,808 group-0 frames (69 of 368 entries, the 17
player-coloured BEWOHNTYPE names). Two storage strategies measured (bytes each, not chosen): one
coloured copy per colour a scene uses, vs. one uncoloured copy + a per-instance colour mask —
both trivial against the headroom found; a performance/complexity trade-off, not a memory one.

**GPU limits** (`--atlas-gpu-limits`, orchestrator's go asked for and given before opening a
device): RTX 4090 (Vulkan) maxTextureDimension2D 32,768 / maxTextureArrayLayers 2,048 /
maxBufferSize 1 TiB; Radeon iGPU (Vulkan) 16,384 / 8,192 / 2 GiB. Neither limit is binding for any
candidate measured. (Correction caught in review: the "4090" adapter-match string is a number,
and `pick_adapter` treats a numeric string as an index, never a name substring — it fell back to
the default adapter, *loudly* (`adapter_from_env`, `wgpu.cpp:164-166`, printed to stderr, and the
limits output names the adapter actually opened) — fixed to match by "RTX"/"Radeon".)

**Layout chosen** (full reasons: `docs/render/atlas.md` §7): `AtlasResidency` (shelf, already
specified, now proven by a one-shot `ensure()` call); page 2048 px; padding 2 px (fits with more
headroom than 4 px; whether 2 px suffices 1c's real dilation kernel is for 1b/1c to confirm, not
measured here); **no mip chain** for the static+water atlas — every mip-including candidate meets
or exceeds the 256 MiB iGPU budget for some worst scene (table in `atlas.md` §3), while the chosen
no-mip layout fits both budgets with headroom; the owner may still add mips on the 4090 alone
(fits with headroom even with them) as a device-specific choice, not decided here. Figures kept in
their own class (Static/Hot split, `gpu-chunks.md` 4.2), not mixed into the static+water budget.

**Tests.** New `residency_test.cpp` case (no game files): hand-computed page counts for a
padding-inflated synthetic set (4 unpadded 30x30 frames pack into 1 layer of 64; the same 4 with 2
px padding need 4, since 34+34 no longer fits 64) plus an oversized-after-padding `Overflow`
check. `anno_render_tests`: 212/213 (the one failure, `scene_reclaim_test.cpp:56`, reproduces
identically — `CHECK(12 == 11)` — on unmodified `origin/main` `ac02d4a2` in a throwaway worktree,
same command (`wsl -d Ubuntu -- anno_render_tests`, default order, right after `river_shade_test`'s
last case): a pre-existing, order-dependent flake, not caused by this change).

**Gates.** `clang-format` 23.1.3 clean on both changed files.
`wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash tools/check_unix_warnings.sh`: GCC 13 and Clang 18, viewer+GPU on, 413
files, clean except the known pre-existing `src/sim/tests/extensions_test.cpp` failure
(`ANNO_EXTENSION_ORACLE_FILE`, untouched by this task, reported in prior sessions' REPORTS); viewer
without GPU, 80 files, clean on both compilers. MSVC Release build clean (warnings as errors).
`git diff --stat origin/main -- src/` shows only `render/tests/residency_test.cpp` and
`tools/bench_frame/main.cpp` — no render-path, digest or picture file touched.

**NOT_RUN.** The whole-suite/game-file runs for other lanes (not reached by this change); macOS
(no host here).

**Decisions and reasoning.**
- Reused `AtlasResidency`'s own `ensure()` as a one-shot full-corpus packer (huge budget, one
  call) rather than simulating per-frame residency with eviction: the task asks for the real page
  count a scene needs resident at once, not an LRU trace, and `ensure()`'s own tallest-first sort
  already makes the result order-independent (existing `residency_test.cpp` case).
- Enumerated every animation frame by calling `animation()`/`frame_index()` directly (their exact,
  cited formula) instead of sampling many `time_ms` values through `place_prepared`: exact, not an
  approximation that depends on choosing a "good enough" time range.
- Mirrored `build_island_lists`'s enhanced-water exclusion (`kSurfAnlage`/`kRiverAnlagen`/
  `kRiverFallAnlagen`) with the same public constants, rather than trusting a `WaterStyle`
  parameter through `prepare_objects` (which does not take one): the exclusion lives in `Scene`,
  not in `prepare_objects` itself.
- `<file>` argument given real meaning (single-scene vs. "-" for the corpus) after review found
  "ignored" unacceptable for a documented option — fixed, not just reworded.
- Decoded the whole Anlagen.dat catalog for the player-colour pixel test via
  `assets::building::to_rgba` (not `figure::decode`) after the first attempt failed every frame:
  Anlagen entries carry `palette_ids` against the file-wide colour table, not the per-entry
  `palettes` FigurenHeader.dat uses — `SpriteCache::get`'s own call site (`iso.cpp:322`) is the
  evidence for which function is the real decode path.
- Page size/padding/mip choices are driven by the measured worst-case fit against both GPUs'
  budgets, not guessed; where a choice remains open (2 px sufficiency for 1c's dilation, mips on
  the 4090 only), it is named as open rather than decided.

**QUESTIONs:** OQ-096 (the 512 MiB/256 MiB budgets themselves) stays open, unchanged by this task.
Whether 2 px padding is enough for 1c's real dilation/upload code is for 1b/1c to confirm.

READY FOR REVIEW.

candidate) against its 256 MiB budget — 16 MiB over, every other candidate worse. QUESTION written
in `atlas.md` §4 (scene, bytes, four options with their costs); not decided here, as instructed.

this padding.** A mip level *n* needs 2ⁿ px of padding or atlas neighbours bleed in; 2 px supports
exactly one level, not a chain (a real chain for a 2048 px page would need 2048 px of padding).
Replaced the `full`/4/3 rows with `one_level`/+25% (`kOneMipLevelFactor`, code comment has the
derivation); re-ran. `atlas.md` §7 now calls the mip level a proposal with the measured facts

both budgets), not a chosen layout value. Added OQ-096b next to OQ-096 for both open decisions
(the mip level, and F1's budget QUESTION).

change the fit conclusion" and the "a few hundred KB to a few MB" estimate. `atlas.md` §5 now says
plainly that `scene.units` is the scenario file's own starting ships/soldiers, not a running game's
carriers/residents/animals/added ships, which the loader cannot see; gives the one number this
measurement can give (the measured maximum across the whole corpus: 3,401,840 bytes / 74 frames,
`Scenes/0201SingleAddOn/single38.sze` group 0) and says the figure class needs its own evicting
budget sized later, from a running game. §6's player-colour byte estimates are marked as resting

frames to find player colour (it matches ordinary grass/trees/painted parts just as readily), not

## LAYER-CHECK-1 — a CTest test keeping formats/sim/sim_load free of app/render/SDL/GPU code — READY FOR REVIEW (task/LAYER-CHECK-1, new worktree from `origin/main` `ac02d4a2`)

**The rule**, stated once in `tools/layer_check.py`'s own module docstring (docs cite it, do not
copy it): `anno_formats` may include/link nothing above it; `anno_sim` may include/link
`anno_formats`; `anno_sim_load` may include/link `anno_sim` (and so `anno_formats` transitively).
Each library's own tests additionally get doctest and `anno/test/...` (the real namespace -
`anno_test_support`'s headers live under `anno/test/`, not `anno/test_support/`, found and fixed
after the first self-test run flagged every test file using it); `anno_sim`'s own tests also get
`anno/sim_load/...` (CMake already links `anno_sim_tests` to `anno_sim_load` for the scenario
corpus case). SDL, webgpu/wgpu, and `anno/render`/`anno/app`/`anno/assets`/`anno/net`/`anno/ui` are
refused everywhere in the three libraries, code and tests alike.

**The link list is read from CMake itself**: `file(GENERATE)` at the end of the root
`CMakeLists.txt` (after all three `add_subdirectory` calls, so the targets already exist) writes
`anno_formats`/`anno_sim`/`anno_sim_load`'s real `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:...,LINK_LIBRARIES>` into
`layer_check_links.txt` in the build directory; `tools/layer_check.py --link-list` reads that file,
never a hand-written copy of the graph.

**The three outcomes of step 5, all confirmed:**
- the real tree passes both checks (`layer_check_contract`, verified via `ctest -R layer_check -V`
  after a configure-only `cmake --preset dev` in WSL, no build needed - both link_libraries and the
  include scan are static/configure-time facts);
- an injected `#include <SDL3/SDL.h>` in a synthetic sim source fails, naming the file and line
  (`--self-test`'s `tree_self_test`);
- a synthetic link list with `anno_render` under `anno_sim` fails (`--self-test`'s link-table
  check).

**Registered** as `layer_check_contract` and `layer_check_self_test`, both `LABELS "workflow"`, so
every job that runs the other workflow tests (`test_verdict_contract` etc.) runs these on Windows,
Linux and macOS alike - no per-platform gating needed, the check is pure Python over text files.

**No violation found in the real tree.** No fix was needed; nothing beyond `CMakeLists.txt`,
`tools/layer_check.py` and the `docs/testing/README.md` section was touched.

**Gates.** `layer_check_contract`/`layer_check_self_test`: 2/2 passed (`ctest -R layer_check -V`,
WSL, 4.3s total). No sim/formats/sim_load source touched, so `anno_sim_tests`/`anno_formats_tests`
were not run (not reached by this change). No C++ touched, so `clang-format` is a no-op, noted
rather than silently skipped.

**Decisions and reasoning:**
- Whitelist, not a blocklist, for the link check (`check_links`): a library may link only what the
  table names, not "anything except the five named upper layers" - catches an unexpected future
  link target the task's own five examples don't name, not just SDL/render/app/assets/net/ui.
- `anno_sim`'s tests keep their existing `anno_sim_load` reach (CMake already wires it for the
  scenario corpus case) rather than treating it as a violation to fix: the task's own step 1 names
  this exact exception ("for the sim tests anno/sim_load").
- `file(GENERATE)` placed after `add_subdirectory(src/sim_load)` (not earlier, where the other
  workflow tests are registered): the generator expression needs the three targets to already
  exist in CMake's model, even though its *value* resolves later, at the generate step.

**NOT_RUN:** the full suite/other lanes (not reached by this change); macOS (no host here; the
test is pure Python, expected to be platform-independent, unverified on that host).

READY FOR REVIEW.

## LAYER-CHECK-1 addendum — the orchestrator's CHANGES REQUESTED review, resolved — READY FOR REVIEW (same branch, new commits)

Review: `docs/orchestration/reviews/2026-11-17-layer-check-1-review.md`, orch/board-next
`f26e03da`. Verdict quoted: **CHANGES REQUESTED**, about 45 minutes. The link check and the
`anno/` rule table were accepted as they were; two findings.

**F1 (a deny list lets anything unnamed through) — rewritten as an allow list.** `classify_include`
now refuses a header unless it is: a C++20 standard library header (`STD_HEADERS`, the full
`cppreference` header index, cited there, not reproduced in prose); the library's own `anno/<lib>/`
area or a library strictly below it; a quoted header that resolves to a real file next to the
including file or inside that library's own `include/`/`tests/` directory (checked by path, not by
name); doctest, in tests; or a `NAMED_EXCEPTIONS` entry scoped to one exact file with its reason.
The real tree's two non-standard, non-`anno/` headers are both named:
`src/sim/tests/founding_assets_test.cpp` uses `<sys/resource.h>` (POSIX `getrusage()`, no Windows
equivalent, already guarded by `#ifndef _WIN32` in the source) and `"freight_original.inc"` (a
generated fixture, included textually, not a real header). A new check
(`check_named_exceptions_are_used`) reports a `NAMED_EXCEPTIONS` entry whose file no longer exists
or no longer includes that header, so the list cannot rot into a claim about a file that moved on.
Added the two required self-test cases (`<vulkan/vulkan.h>`, `<windows.h>` in a synthetic sim
source both fail, named with file and line) plus one more in the same spirit
(`<GLFW/glfw3.h>`, an unlisted third-party header, is refused by default - the exact thing an
allow list is for that a deny list would have missed). The real tree still passes outright.

**F2 (the section landed inside "Pins and goldens", and over-cited) — fixed.** The new
`docs/testing/README.md` section had been inserted after that section's own closing code-block
paragraph but *before* its numbered regeneration steps continued (1-7, ending "Finish with
check"), so those steps were rendering under the new heading instead of their own. Moved the
section to the true end of the file, after step 7. Dropped "and CLAUDE.md" from the citation:
CLAUDE.md does not cite `tools/layer_check.py`, and an executor does not edit CLAUDE.md to make it
do so.

**Gates re-run after the code change:** `layer_check_self_test` (now covering the allow-list
rewrite, the named-exception staleness check, and the three required-failing synthetic cases) and
`layer_check_contract` (the real tree, via the link-list file already generated from the earlier
configure - no new `cmake`/build/WSL run needed, per the standing hold on PC-heavy work during the
landing candidate's own build): both pass, run directly with `python3 -I tools/layer_check.py`
(no WSL, under a second each).

**Decisions and reasoning:**
- `STD_HEADERS` lists the *whole* C++20 standard library header index, not only the headers the
  tree happens to use today: a future, legitimate standard-header use then needs no rule change,
  matching the task's own "the standard library" wording rather than a narrower "headers seen so
  far" list that would need updating on every new include.
- The quoted-header allowance is resolved by real filesystem path (`.is_file()`), not by comparing
  names against a list of known test-helper filenames: there are dozens of these (`cloth_town.hpp`,
  `command_helpers.hpp`, ...) and a name-based list would itself rot the moment a new one is added,
  the exact failure mode F1 was raised to prevent.
- `NAMED_EXCEPTIONS` is keyed by `(file, header)`, not by header alone: a future file that happens
  to want the same non-standard header still needs its own entry and its own reason, rather than
  silently inheriting someone else's justification.

READY FOR REVIEW.

## FLAKE-RESIZE-1 — paused on the owner's instruction, mid-proof — PAUSED (task/FLAKE-RESIZE-1, from origin/main `4dfdd9b7`, head `b3304fd1`)

**Stopped here, not finished, on the owner's explicit instruction to halt all work until the next day.** No new step started after this message arrived; what follows records exactly where the task stands.

**Root cause, found and fixed, with CI-confirmed evidence.** `anno_app_input_tests`' ZOOM-SMOOTH-2b F1 case (`src/app/tests/live_resize_test.cpp`) failed once in CI (run 44076929673, attempt 1, `linux-clang-asan`) with a LeakSanitizer report, not a correctness/race failure - all 4 doctest assertions in that case passed. Cause: the case's background `std::thread` floods `SDL_PushEvent` with nothing draining the queue; SDL 3.4.18's own `SDL_AddEvent` (`SDL_events.c`, the pinned source, read directly) refuses and calls `SDL_SetError` once the queue already holds `SDL_MAX_QUEUED_EVENTS` (65535, a hard cap). `SDL_SetError` lazily allocates a per-thread TLS error buffer (`SDL_GetErrBuf`) that SDL only frees for threads it created itself (`SDL_CreateThread`); this is a raw `std::thread`, so the buffer leaked whenever a slow/contended CI run happened to push past 65535 within the test's own ~10 ms window - the flakiness.

**Fix, in two commits for the proof the task asked for.**
- Commit A (`333b6035`): the pusher now pushes a fixed 70,000 events before its normal loop, forcing the overflow deterministically regardless of timing - with `SDL_CleanupTLS()` deliberately NOT called yet. Pushed; CI run **44177906209**'s `linux-clang-asan` job failed with the identical leak signature (214 bytes, 4 allocations, `SDL_GetErrBuf`) - confirmed via the job's own uploaded `test.log` artifact, not just the summary line. Every other job in that run passed - this one case is the only thing the fix touches.
- Commit B (`b3304fd1`, current head): restores `SDL_CleanupTLS()` at the end of the pusher lambda, with a comment quoting SDL 3.4.18's own `SDL_thread.h` doc text verbatim. Pushed; **CI on this head has not been checked yet** (the halt instruction arrived before it could complete) - this is the one outstanding verification.

**Local WSL ASan proof: blocked, then started, not finished.**
- First attempt (before packages were installed): WSL Ubuntu was missing all X11/Wayland/audio dev packages CI installs except `libx11-dev`; SDL3's own cmake configure refused. Reported to the orchestrator; held rather than using `SDL_UNIX_CONSOLE_BUILD=ON` (would diverge from CI's own configuration).
- Owner installed the 20 missing packages (`dpkg --configure -a` first for an interrupted state). Reconfigured and built `anno_app_input_tests` (ASan preset) successfully - but with the **default compiler** (`/usr/bin/c++`, GCC), not Clang: the commit-A binary then passed 15/15 local runs, i.e. did **not** reproduce the leak locally, because CI's `linux-clang-asan` job specifically uses Clang, and GCC's own sanitizer runtime did not report it here.
- Rebuilt with the standalone Clang 18 at `/home/altin/clang18/root/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/clang++` (the same compiler `tools/check_unix_warnings.sh` uses for its compile-only checks) to match CI. Configure and **compiling** succeeded, but **linking** `anno_budget_coord` (a dependency built before `anno_app_input_tests` in the same ninja graph) failed: `/usr/bin/ld: cannot find .../libclang_rt.asan-x86_64.a` (and the `_static`/`_cxx` variants) - this standalone Clang installation has no compiler-rt sanitizer runtime libraries, only enough to compile (consistent with `check_unix_warnings.sh`'s own compile-only use of it). **Never got to actually run the binary with this compiler**; the local WSL Clang ASan proof is NOT_RUN for this reason, distinct from the earlier X11/Wayland blocker.
- CI runs 44076929673 (the original flaky failure, attempt 1) and 44177906209 (commit A's deterministic failure) stand as the substitute evidence for the local WSL proof, per the orchestrator's own instruction once the compiler gap was found.

**Not started at all: the Windows msvc 50-loop stability proof (item 3) and the second item (`viewer_wiring_r4_occupancy`, 50 loops, item 4).** `anno_app_input_tests` was built once on msvc Release (confirms the code compiles there) but no loop was run - the halt arrived first.

**Cleanup done before stopping:** no background build, test loop, or WSL process left running (checked `pgrep` in WSL and `Get-Process` on Windows for ninja/cc1plus/clang++/cmake/ctest/anno_* after each step); the detached gatecheck worktree and its two scratch WSL build directories (`~/anno-build/flake-resize-1-check`, `~/anno-build/flake-resize-1-check-clang`) were removed.

**What's next, for whoever resumes:**
1. Check CI on head `b3304fd1` (commit B) - should be fully green; if not, read why before anything else.
2. Either get this standalone Clang 18 a compiler-rt runtime (or find/install a different Clang 18 that has one) to actually run the local WSL ASan loop proof, or treat CI runs 44076929673/44177906209 as sufficient per the orchestrator's own fallback instruction and say so explicitly in the final report.
3. Run the msvc 50-loop stability proof (`anno_app_input_tests`/live_resize, confirming the 70,000 forced pushes keep the test's own assertions stable) and the `viewer_wiring_r4_occupancy` 50-loop (item 4), neither started yet.
4. `check_unix_warnings.sh` has not been run against this branch's change yet either.

## RENDER-DIRECT-1b — the resident atlas pages, built on the CPU, proven texel-exact, every gate green — READY FOR REVIEW (task/RENDER-DIRECT-1b, from `origin/task/RENDER-DIRECT-1a` `5fb98192`, merged `origin/main` `09315620` then `4dfdd9b7`, head `c550124f`)

**The unit and its interface.** New `anno_render` unit `src/render/include/anno/render/atlas_pages.hpp`,
`src/render/src/atlas_pages.cpp`: `build_atlas_pages(frames, page_size, padding, threads) -> AtlasPages`.
`AtlasFrameInput{id, image}` in, one call to the existing `AtlasResidency::ensure`/`place` for packing (no
second packer), then per-frame texel work on `threads` workers. `AtlasPages{level0, level1, placements,
oversized, duplicate_ids}`: `level0`/`level1` are `page_size`²/`(page_size/2)`² RGBA8 buffers per layer;
`placements` gives each frame's layer/x/y/width/height at both levels; `oversized`/`duplicate_ids` name
anything not placed, never dropped silently. Nothing here is read by any render path yet (RENDER-DIRECT-1c
uploads and draws from these pages).

**Rounding rules, each cited.** Premultiply: `c' = (c·a + 127) / 255` per channel, integer, half up
(`premultiply_pixel`) - round to nearest for every input, since 255 is odd and no product lands on a half
(review, confirmed). Dilation: every slot texel outside the frame copies the nearest frame texel, clamped
to the edge, premultiplied the same way. One mip level: each level-1 texel is the 2×2 box of level 0,
summed per channel and rounded half up, `(s + 2) / 4`.

**Thread safety, reasoned and proven.** Every slot's width/height is rounded up to the next even number
before packing, so every slot's own origin is also even and the page-wide mip grid never has to average
texels from two different frames' slots at a boundary - the fact that makes per-frame worker threads safe
with no shared lock on the per-texel path. Proven by a hash-equality test (1 vs. 8 threads, 200 synthetic
frames and, separately, a duplicated-id case).

**Step 1, the budget default.** `cb_atlas_budget_bytes`'s 256 MiB non-discrete default is now 384 MiB
(OQ-096); the default-and-clamp logic is `atlas_budget_bytes_before_sprite(atlas_budget_mb, adapter_type,
max_layers, layer_bytes)` (`gpu.hpp`), a pure function `cb_atlas_budget_bytes` (`gpu.cpp`) calls. 9/9
assertions, no GPU device opened.

**Step 4, the texel-exact proof, every frame, every scene the packet names.**
- **Synthetic** (`atlas_pages_test.cpp`): 1×1, odd sizes, a frame exactly filling a page, alpha 0/255
  edges, the thread-hash case, a duplicated-id case (review F3), a case asserting the mip rectangle fields
  directly on an even- and an odd-sized frame (review F4). 8 `TEST_CASE`s, **120/120 assertions**.
- **Game files**, split by what each scene needs to load (orchestrator, after F2): `Scenes/0010SingleEndlos/
  02_1024_easy_128.sze` and `Scenes/0100Kampagne01/S01_01_01.sze` stay in `anno_render_tests`
  (`atlas_pages_corpus_test.cpp`); `data/maps/lan5.txt` moved to `anno_app_tests`
  (`atlas_pages_lan5_test.cpp`) - a fixed map needs `app::load_play`/`load_placed_scene`, and
  `anno_render_tests` must not depend on `anno_app_core` to stay below it (`anno_render_gpu_tests`'s own
  link is the one, pre-existing exception, not a precedent to extend). The frame-gathering and the checker
  (`collect_static_water`, `check_pages_against_source`) live in one shared header,
  `anno/test/atlas_pages_check.hpp` (`src/test_support`, header-only - test_support's own library gets no
  render/assets dependency), included by both binaries instead of copied. **Every frame, every level-0
  texel of its own rectangle, and every texel of its own mip rectangle checked against the decoder
  directly** (review F2: an earlier revision sampled every 7th frame and excluded `lan5.txt` on a
  proportionality call that turned out to rest on an unreleased Debug build's own timing - both reverted;
  the deviation should have gone to the orchestrator before being built, not reported afterward). Native
  MSVC Release, `ANNO1503_GAME_DIR` set: the two `.sze` scenes **50,755,526/50,755,526 assertions**;
  `lan5.txt` **39,965,981/39,965,981 assertions**.

**No frame found unequal.** 0 failures across every proof case above.

**A dangling-buffer bug, found twice, same class, both in this task's own new test code.** First:
`sze::Scene::parse(read_all(sze_file))` fed a temporary straight into `parse()`; `formats::sze::Scene` holds
spans into it, not a copy. Second, while debugging the first: `fig::FigurenHeader::parse(read_all(dir /
"FigurenHeader.dat"))`, same pattern - `formats::figuren::Entry` holds spans too. Both fixed by binding a
named buffer first; confirmed under AddressSanitizer and the plain build. Exhaustively grepped every call
site of `FigurenHeader::parse`/`AnlagenFile::parse`/`sze::Scene::parse`/`insel::islands`/`TexFile::parse`
across `src/` and `tools/`: no other instance anywhere, in engine code or otherwise.

**Step 5, the bench table (`bench_frame --atlas-build <scene|-> out.tsv`), Release numbers (review F1).**
The first numbers were measured on the `dev`/WSL preset, which is `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` Debug
(`CMakePresets.json:10`) against `docs/perf/README.md`'s own Release convention - a real mistake, caught
before this branch's first push could be trusted. Rerun on the native `msvc` Release build, the same

groups 0+1+2 at 2048 px/2 px/one_level, plus the 10 rows nearest the sorted median index of 519) plus

across the 20-scene subset, 0 mismatches (F1's own free consistency check).** Every wall-time number below
is the Release figure, about 19-24x faster than the retired Debug numbers on the same scenes (e.g.
`endless02.sze` 27.45 s -> 1.30 s; `lan5.txt` 12.84 s build / 1m37s wall (app-layer load included) -> 0.70

| | static+water bytes (the Static-class budget's own figure) | figures bytes | total wall | collect | pack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| worst 10 | 280.0-360.0 MiB | 20.0 MiB (every scene, 1 page) | 0.84-1.30 s | 0.76-1.20 s | 0.068-0.100 s |
| median 10 | 80.0-140.0 MiB | 0 (no start units on these `.scp` templates) | 0.18-0.36 s | 0.15-0.32 s | 0.022-0.038 s |

**Finding, confirmed in Release: `collect` dominates, not `pack`, 85.3-92.4% of static wall time** (median
90.1%) across all 22 scenes - the same shape as the retired Debug numbers (88-94%, median 90.8%): the
balance between the two phases does not depend on optimisation level, even though the absolute times do
(both sped up by roughly the same factor). `pack` is genuinely parallel (`static_cpu_ms` still exceeds
wall time on every scene) but too small a share to matter. Not fixed here (step 5's "no blind
optimisation"): named as a RENDER-DIRECT-1c finding - `FrameTable`/`SpriteCache` are already thread-safe
(`shared_mutex`, both), the same primitives `build_atlas_pages`'s own worker split already uses, so
`collect`'s per-island/per-group traversal could be split the same way with no new synchronization design.

**Review F5, resolved: the iGPU's own adjacent-pair case, from real decoded pages - both pairs hold, no
finding for the owner.** `--atlas-build` now also builds groups {0,1} and {1,2} separately per scene
(`collect_static_water_groups`, generalised from an all-three-groups-only helper to take any group list).
Worst pair 0+1: **340.0 MiB** (`endless02.sze`) against the iGPU's 384 MiB - **44 MiB headroom**, matching
1a's own sizing-only estimate for this quantity almost exactly (same figure, a different specific scene).
Worst pair 1+2: only **100.0 MiB** (`01_1024_easy_256.sze`). Neither pair exceeds 384 MiB anywhere measured.

**Peak process memory**, Release, across all 22 scenes: **1,645,867,008 bytes (1,569.6 MiB, `endless02.sze`)**
worst, 545.0 MiB (`D_080x080_0016_2B_Afrika.scp`) least - **higher** than the retired Debug run's own worst
(967 MiB, the same scene): plausible and not investigated further - Release finishes about 20x faster, so
more of the run's own transient allocations are live at the same instant rather than freed between them.

**Separately, own commit: `play_gpu_test.cpp:75`'s `MESSAGE` streamed a `const char* adapter_name` raw,
printing its address instead of its text - fixed with `std::string(adapter_name)`.**

**No render-path or draw-call change.** Touched: `atlas_pages.hpp/.cpp` (new), `atlas_pages_test.cpp`/
`atlas_pages_corpus_test.cpp` (new/revised), `atlas_pages_lan5_test.cpp` (new, `anno_app_tests`),

## RENDER-DIRECT-1c — the resident atlas pages uploaded to the GPU, proven exact by readback and sampling, both adapters — READY FOR REVIEW (task/RENDER-DIRECT-1c, from `origin/task/RENDER-DIRECT-1b` `95a5ace6`, head `cf9e2cc4`)

**The unit.** New `anno_render_gpu` module, `src/render/include/anno/render/atlas_upload.hpp` /
`src/render/src/atlas_upload.cpp`: opens no device of its own (the caller's `gpu::Context`) and touches no
`GpuFrame` state - "a new unit, not a change to the chunk compositor" (the packet's own words, confirmed by
`git diff` against the task base: nothing under `GpuFrame::render`, the chunk build, the viewer, `--png`, or
any digest changed). `upload_atlas_pages(ctx, pages, budget_bytes)` makes one 2D texture array, RGBA8Unorm
(matching the existing sprite atlas's format family, `new_atlas`/`gpu.cpp` - never `*Srgb`, `GpuFrame::
create`'s own "a sRGB target would convert twice" rule), `page_size` x `page_size` x `pages.level0.size()`
layers, **2 mip levels** written straight from `AtlasPages::level0`/`level1` (no GPU-generated mips - that
would silently redo RENDER-DIRECT-1b's own box filter, untested against it). Usage `TextureBinding | CopyDst
| CopySrc` (`CopySrc` for the readback proof).

**The refusal, named not truncated.** `atlas_upload_refusal(layers, page_size, max_array_layers,
max_dimension_2d, needed_bytes, budget_bytes)` - a pure function, no device, checked against three
conditions in order (no layers / layer count over `maxTextureArrayLayers` / page size over
`maxTextureDimension2D` / `atlas_pages_bytes(pages)` over `budget_bytes`); `upload_atlas_pages` reads the
real device's limits and calls this for the decision, so the decision itself is unit-tested with zero GPU
(the packet's own acceptance item).

**Which groups: `resident_atlas_groups(adapter_type, zoom_group, group_count)`.** A discrete adapter holds
every group (ADR 0007 decision 2); any other adapter holds the pair `{zoom_group, zoom_group + 1}`, clamped
to `group_count - 2` at the top of the range, a single group when `group_count <= 1`. Pure and total, tested
without a GPU for discrete/integrated/CPU/unknown adapter kinds and `group_count` in {0, 1, 2, 3}.
**Resolved the orchestrator's review question** (why `zoom_group + 1` and never `zoom_group - 1`): derived
from `docs/render/iso.md`'s own "Choosing the level" hysteresis mechanism - while the picture is shown on
group g, the continuous zoom position is bounded so it is always strictly between `tile_w(g)` and
`tile_w(g + 1)`, never between `tile_w(g)` and `tile_w(g - 1)` (that interval is where the picture has
already switched to `g - 1`, since the scale on `g` there would exceed `max_upscale`). So `g + 1` is the
only neighbour `g` can be adjacent to while `g` is the group shown, not an arbitrary pick between two
equally plausible ones. Full derivation in `docs/render/atlas.md` section 11.

**The placement-to-UV rule: `sample_placement`, realized as `textureLoad`, no sampler.** Every pass in
`gpu.wgsl` already reads a resident texture with `textureLoad` only, never a filtered sampler
("textureLoad, never filtered, so cached chunks and sprites stay exact", `gpu.wgsl`'s own comment); no
`WGPUSampler` object exists anywhere in this codebase. The new shader `src/render/shaders/atlas_upload.wgsl`
follows that convention: `textureLoad(atlas_tex, origin + floor(pos.xy), layer, level)` at the destination
pixel's own integer index - exact at every texel, the nearest-sampler-at-texel-centres rule the packet asks
for, with the rounding ambiguity a true sampler could introduce at a rectangle's edge removed by
construction.

**Readback (step 2) and sampling (step 3): both proofs, both adapters, by name (`ANNO_GPU_ADAPTER=RTX` /
the Radeon iGPU, `play_gpu_test.cpp`'s own adapter-pinning pattern reused as `on_named_adapter`).**
- Synthetic (4 placements - 1x1, odd size, alpha edges, a larger frame): readback and sampling both exact on
  the 4090 and the Radeon.
- `data/maps/lan5.txt`'s static+water: every group on the 4090 (3 groups, 1090 placements/pass,
  **39,966,623 assertions**), the adjacent pair {0,1} on the Radeon (`resident_atlas_groups(IntegratedGPU,
  0, 3)`, 2 groups, **38,094,953 assertions**) - readback and sampling both exact on both adapters.
- `Scenes/0010SingleEndlos/02_1024_easy_128.sze` groups 0+1 (the worst adjacent pair, 340 MiB,
  RENDER-DIRECT-1b review F5's own finding), readback only (the packet names this dataset for step 2, not
  step 3): exact on both adapters.

`ctx.errors` checked at 0 after every case. Neither adapter needed `ANNO_REQUIRE_GPU` - both were present
and opened cleanly throughout.

**Step 4, measured on the orchestrator's quiet-PC slot (confirmed idle first: no `check_unix_warnings`/
`cc1plus`/`clang` in WSL, no `cl.exe`/`ctest`/`cmake`/`anno_*`/`MSBuild` on Windows), `msvc` Release,
`ANNO1503_GAME_DIR` set, both real adapters by name:**

| Scene | Adapter | Groups resident | Layers | VRAM (upload only) | Upload (fenced) | Readback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lan5.txt | RTX 4090 (all 3) | 0,1,2 | 10 | 200.0 MiB | 22.74 ms | 117.02 ms |
| lan5.txt | Radeon iGPU (adjacent pair) | 0,1 | 9 | 180.0 MiB | 78.18 ms | 70.12 ms |
| 02_1024_easy_128.sze worst pair | RTX 4090 | 0,1 (separate) | 1+1 | 40.0 MiB | 4.62 ms | 11.65 ms |
| 02_1024_easy_128.sze worst pair | Radeon iGPU | 0,1 (separate) | 1+1 | 40.0 MiB | 2.76 ms | 16.75 ms |

Per-layer VRAM (20,971,520 B at `page_size = 2048`) matches `atlas_pages_bytes`'s own formula exactly - no
device-vs-formula discrepancy to account for. The Radeon's upload is slower than the 4090's on the largest
group (74.77 ms vs. 16.63 ms, 7 layers) - expected for an integrated part without the 4090's discrete memory
bandwidth; its readback is faster on that same group (56.52 ms vs. 98.96 ms), plausibly because `mapAsync`
over its unified-memory heap skips the 4090's discrete-VRAM copy-back (not investigated further - a wall-
time observation, not a correctness claim). Neither adapter's `maxTextureArrayLayers`/`maxTextureDimension2D`
binds at these layer counts. Full tables in `docs/render/atlas.md` section 11 and `docs/perf/README.md`.

**No render-path or draw-call change.** Touched: `atlas_upload.hpp`/`.cpp` (new, `anno_render_gpu`),
`atlas_upload.wgsl` (new shader), `atlas_upload_test.cpp` (new, `anno_render_gpu_tests`), one `shaders.hpp`/
`CMakeLists.txt` embed-text entry (`anno_embed_text`, following `gpu.wgsl`/`fluid.wgsl`'s own pattern), docs.
Nothing under `GpuFrame::render`, the chunk build, the viewer, `--png`, or any digest changed; the existing
GPU test suite (127 pre-existing cases) passed unchanged alongside the new ones.

**Decisions and reasoning.**
- Extracted `atlas_upload_refusal` as a separate pure function from `upload_atlas_pages` (which needs a
  device for `wgpuDeviceGetLimits`) specifically so the refusal decision is unit-tested with zero GPU - the
  packet's own acceptance item, not achievable if the check stayed inline in the device-reading function.
- Reused `play_gpu_test.cpp`'s adapter-pinning pattern (`on_named_adapter`: pin by name, skip if absent, fail
  only under `ANNO_REQUIRE_GPU`) rather than inventing a second one.
- No `WGPUSampler` object introduced: `sample_placement` realizes "nearest sampler, texel centres" as an
  exact `textureLoad`, following the codebase's existing textureLoad-only convention rather than being the
  first caller to add a sampler.
- Resolved the orchestrator's pair-neighbour question from first principles (`iso.md`'s own hysteresis
  bound), not by picking a plausible-sounding default - `g + 1` is provably the only neighbour possible
  while `g` is shown, not a 50/50 guess between `g - 1` and `g + 1`.
- No change to `GpuFrame::render` or any existing shader: the new shader module and the new C++ unit are
  additive, so the existing 127-case suite needed no update to accommodate this task, only to keep passing.
- No guesses went to `open-questions.md`: every design choice here traces either to the packet text itself
  or to existing codebase/doc evidence (`iso.md`, `gpu.wgsl`'s own comment, `GpuFrame::create`'s own sRGB
  rule, `play_gpu_test.cpp`'s own pinning pattern) - none of it is a genuine open question.

**Gates.**
- clang-format 23.1.3: clean on every touched file (one self-inflicted mishap during development - running
  clang-format over `src/render/CMakeLists.txt` by accident mangled it into pseudo-C++ formatting; caught via
  the disk-change diff, `git checkout`-reverted, both intended edits redone by hand with `Edit`, not
  reformatted again).
- WSL GCC 13 / Clang 18 `-Werror`, whole tree, all four configurations (GCC/Clang, viewer+GPU on and off):
  clean.
- `anno_render_gpu_tests`, native MSVC Release, `ANNO_GPU_ADAPTER=RTX`, full suite: **129/129 test cases,
  80,512,304/80,512,304 assertions, 0 failed**, adapter named throughout ("NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
  (Vulkan)").
- `anno_render_gpu_tests`, native MSVC Release, every Radeon-named case (`--test-case=*Radeon*`, default
  adapter selection): **4/4 test cases, 38,095,006/38,095,006 assertions, 0 failed**, adapter named
  throughout ("AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics (Vulkan)").
- Step 4's two measurement cases ran alone, as asked: the shared PC was checked idle first (recorded above),
  the orchestrator was told once each check and once the run was done.
- CI preflight (`python -I tools/test/run_selected.py --preflight-only`, the exact CI step): PASS.

(`Scenes/0011SingleEndlosAddon/endless02.sze`) as both the worst adjacent-pair scene (groups 0+1,
340 MiB) and the worst all-three-group scene (360 MiB), so the real worst case had never been
uploaded. Now uploads `endless02.sze`'s real resident set as ONE combined page set per adapter -
every group `resident_atlas_groups` names folded into one shared `FrameTable`/`SpriteCache` (the
last call's own return already holds every earlier group's frames too, since `collect_static_
water`'s final pass walks the whole table from id 0 - exactly `bench_frame`'s own
`collect_static_water_groups`, the function RD-1b's 340/360 MiB figures were measured with, not a
different method): all three groups (18 layers, 360 MiB) on the 4090, the adjacent pair {0,1} (17
layers, 340 MiB) on the Radeon.

**F2, fixed: a real device budget, not a tautology.** Every budget passed to `upload_atlas_pages`
in this file was `atlas_pages_bytes(pages)` - always exactly what is being uploaded, so the
refusal path was never exercised by a real number. The `endless02.sze` case now computes the real
budget the compositor would compute on the opened device: `atlas_budget_bytes_before_sprite` from
`wgpuDeviceGetLimits`'s own `maxTextureArrayLayers`, the per-frame sprite (Hot) atlas's own
footprint stated as 0 bytes (this standalone unit test holds no `GpuFrame`/Hot atlas of its own to
measure a real one from - the same convention RD-1b's own F5 finding already used for its CPU-side
44 MiB (Radeon)/152 MiB (4090) headroom figures, so this proves those already-accepted numbers
hold for a real GPU upload, not a new, tighter claim). Needed vs. allowed is reported via
`MESSAGE` on every run: RTX 4090 needed 377,487,360 against 536,870,912 allowed; Radeon needed
356,515,840 against 402,653,184 allowed. One new case, `refused_one_byte_short`, proves a budget
one byte short is refused through `upload_atlas_pages` itself (not only the pure
`atlas_upload_refusal` tested without a GPU), on both adapters.

**Finding for the owner, surfaced by F1/F2 together, not a bug in the fix: the Radeon's calculated
budget fits, but the real device still refuses the allocation.** `endless02.sze`'s real pair on
the Radeon needs 356,515,840 bytes, *inside* the calculated 402,653,184-byte budget - the
arithmetic says it fits - but `wgpuDeviceCreateTexture` itself refused the single 17-layer texture
with "Not enough memory left". This is the review's own anticipated category ("that's a finding
for the owner, not a fix") under a different failure signature than expected: a real
single-allocation ceiling below the device's own configured/reported memory, not a
budget-arithmetic overrun. **Recorded, not patched: a calculated budget that fits is necessary but
not sufficient on this adapter - a resident set this large needs either more than one texture
resource (a stage 2/3 upload-granularity design question, explicitly out of this packet's "no
draw pass/streaming" scope) or a smaller real budget than 384 MiB to actually allocate as one
texture on this hardware.** The RTX 4090 uploaded the full 18-layer, 360 MiB set with no issue -
the same combined-upload method, a different real limit.

**A second, genuine bug found and fixed while investigating, not merely a reporting gap.**
`upload_atlas_pages` had no error scope around `wgpuDeviceCreateTexture`/`wgpuQueueWriteTexture`:
on the real device refusal above, the WGPU handle came back non-null but device-invalidated, and
the function returned `out` as a *success* holding it - the caller (`check_pages_on_gpu`) then
tried to read it back and hit a byte-mismatch `REQUIRE` failure, not a named refusal, which would
have misreported a real allocation failure as a readback/correctness bug in this task's own proof.
Fixed by wrapping both the texture creation and every `wgpuQueueWriteTexture` call in one
validation + out-of-memory error scope (`submit`'s own push/pop pattern, reused), returning a
descriptive error naming the layers/needed/budgeted bytes when either scope catches something.
Confirmed fixed by rerunning the Radeon case: it now returns the clean, named refusal shown above
instead of a readback mismatch.

**Test case name/structure changes.** `check_pages_on_gpu` lost its `budget_bytes` parameter
(every remaining caller always passes the tautological budget, so the parameter was dead weight
after the refactor below) and gained a sibling, `verify_readback` (the byte-for-byte readback loop
alone, extracted so `worst_pair_scene` can call it on an already-uploaded texture after handling
its own, possibly-refused upload separately - `check_pages_on_gpu` itself is unchanged for every
other caller). The two `02_1024_easy_128.sze`-named `TEST_CASE`s are renamed to name
`endless02.sze` and the real finding (all three groups / the adjacent pair, not "340 MiB" as a
flat label repeated for both scenes). Two new `TEST_CASE`s (`refused_one_byte_short` on each
adapter).

**Gates, rerun on this commit.**
- clang-format 23.1.3: clean on all three touched files.
- WSL GCC 13 / Clang 18 `-Werror`, whole tree, all four configurations: clean.
- `anno_render_gpu_tests`, native MSVC Release, `ANNO_GPU_ADAPTER=RTX`, full suite: **131/131 test
  cases, 80,512,458/80,512,458 assertions, 0 failed** (122 pre-existing cases unchanged, 9 of this
  file's own, 2 more than the previous round's 7 - the `endless02.sze` pair is now one case per
  adapter instead of none, plus `refused_one_byte_short` per adapter).
- `anno_render_gpu_tests`, native MSVC Release, every Radeon-named case (`--test-case=*Radeon*`,
  default adapter selection): **5/5 test cases, 38,095,006/38,095,006 assertions, 0 failed**
  (one more than the previous round: `refused_one_byte_short` on the Radeon).
- CI preflight: PASS.
- These are correctness runs (no quiet-PC slot requested or needed, per the review's own note);
  the step 4 timing rows from the previous round are untouched and still indicative/measured as

**Decisions and reasoning.**
- Combined every resident group into ONE page set for `endless02.sze` (not one upload per group,
  as the previous revision did for `02_1024_easy_128.sze`) because that is what any adapter
  actually holds resident at once - uploading groups separately would not have reproduced RD-1b's

  above (which only appears for the single large resource, not for two smaller separate ones - the

- Took the per-frame sprite atlas's footprint as 0 bytes, stated and documented, rather than
  building a real `GpuFrame`/Hot atlas inside this standalone unit test to measure one: matches
  RD-1b's own F5 convention exactly, keeps this unit test free of a `GpuFrame` dependency (the
  task's own "a new unit, not a change to the chunk compositor" boundary), and is explicitly named

- Reported the real device refusal as a finding, not a workaround: did not shrink the upload, did

- Fixed the error-scope gap in `upload_atlas_pages` because it is a real correctness bug in this
  task's own code, found while making the F1/F2 fix honestly report what the real device did -
  not fixing it would have let a genuine device refusal masquerade as a readback/correctness
  failure in this unit's own proof, which is exactly the kind of silent-wrongness CLAUDE.md's

- Left the step 4 timing section of this report and `docs/perf/README.md` untouched: the review

## RENDER-DIRECT-1d — the Radeon's real allocation ceiling, measured and diagnosed — READY FOR REVIEW (task/RENDER-DIRECT-1d, from `origin/task/RENDER-DIRECT-1c` `f148638e`, new worktree)

**Scope, as the packet asked: measurement and diagnosis only.** No production code changed; OQ-096b's 384 MiB non-discrete default is NOT touched. One new file, `src/render/tests/adapter_memory_diag_test.cpp` (`anno_render_gpu_tests`), answering the orchestrator's three questions about RENDER-DIRECT-1c review F1/F2's Radeon finding (`endless02.sze`'s real pair, 356,515,840 bytes, fits the calculated 402,653,184-byte budget but the real device still refuses the single 17-layer texture: "Not enough memory left").

**Question 1, answered: a single-resource ceiling, not the heap's own total capacity - but small enough that even one of the two groups alone can exceed it.** `endless02.sze`'s pair uploaded as two SEPARATE per-group textures: group 1 (4 layers, 83,886,080 bytes/80.0 MiB) allocated; group 0 (14 layers, 293,601,280 bytes/280.0 MiB) was refused even on its own. Splitting the pair by zoom group is not always enough to make a resident set fit.

**Question 2, answered: DXGI's own memory facts** (`DXGI_ADAPTER_DESC`/`IDXGIAdapter1::GetDesc1`, matched to the already-opened wgpu adapter by `vendorID`/`deviceID` - `WGPUAdapterInfo`/webgpu.h has no memory-size fields at all):

| Adapter | DedicatedVideoMemory | DedicatedSystemMemory | SharedSystemMemory |
|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 4090 | 25,310,527,488 B (24,138.0 MiB) | 0 | 16,704,471,040 B (15,930.6 MiB) |
| Radeon iGPU | 488,390,656 B (465.8 MiB) | 0 | 16,704,471,040 B (15,930.6 MiB, same shared pool) |

**Question 3, answered: the real single-resource ceiling, found by bisecting the layer count of a single 2048×2048 texture array with RENDER-DIRECT-1c's own error-scope detection: 12 layers (251,658,240 bytes, 240.0 MiB) allocate on the Radeon; 13 layers (272,629,760 bytes, 260.0 MiB) are refused.** Consistent with question 1 (group 1 at 80.0 MiB well under, group 0 at 280.0 MiB well over), and about **52% of the 465.8 MiB `DedicatedVideoMemory`** DXGI reports for this adapter (question 2) - a real allocator-level restriction, not simply "the dedicated VRAM is smaller than the budget."

**For the owner, prepared not decided: `docs/open-questions.md` OQ-727.** OQ-096b's 384 MiB non-discrete default is well above the real ~240 MiB single-resource ceiling found on this adapter. Three non-exclusive options, none implemented: (a) lower the non-discrete default below the real per-resource ceiling; (b) split any resident set above a configured per-resource size into more than one texture at upload time (a stage 2/3 upload-granularity design, separate from the *total* budget number); (c) measure the real ceiling at runtime per-adapter instead of hardcoding a number that is specific to this PC's Radeon/driver/Vulkan combination on 2026-11-17 and may not transfer elsewhere.

**Gates.**
- clang-format 23.1.3: clean.
- WSL GCC 13 / Clang 18 `-Werror`, whole tree, all four configurations: clean.
- `anno_render_gpu_tests`, native MSVC Release, `ANNO_GPU_ADAPTER=RTX`, full suite: **134/134 test cases, 80,512,071/80,512,071 assertions, 0 failed** (131 pre-existing plus this file's own 3 diagnostic cases - the DXGI case runs both adapters by name within itself).
- `anno_render_gpu_tests`, native MSVC Release, every Radeon-named case (`--test-case=*Radeon*`, default adapter selection): **8/8 test cases, 38,095,019/38,095,019 assertions, 0 failed**.
- CI preflight: PASS.
- No quiet slot needed or requested, per the packet's own note (allocation outcomes, not timings).

**Decisions and reasoning.**
- Tolerated a real device refusal as a reportable finding, not a hard test failure, for both the per-group split (question 1) and the bisection's own expected refusals (question 3's `layers_allocate` just returns a bool) - following RENDER-DIRECT-1c review F1/F2's own precedent: a real, named device outcome is data for the owner, not a bug in the proof, as long as it is the SPECIFIC named refusal expected (checked where it matters) and not some other, unexplained failure.
- Built the bisection's probe pages as all-zero dummy buffers (`dummy_pages`) rather than real decoded scene frames: allocation-size testing needs only the right byte counts, and a real-frame version would have made every bisection step as slow as a full scene decode for no added evidence.
- Called `wait_idle` after every bisection probe so a released texture's memory has a chance to be reclaimed before the next attempt - without it, back-to-back allocate/release cycles could show stale pressure and report a falsely low ceiling.
- Duplicated `on_named_adapter`/`read_all`/`load_scene_direct` from `atlas_upload_test.cpp` rather than sharing them: both files already duplicate small per-binary helpers by this project's own established convention (`atlas_upload_test.cpp`'s own doc comment on `load_scene_direct`), and a new header for helpers only two files in one binary use would be more machinery than the ~30 lines it replaces.
- Added DXGI as a Windows-only diagnostic dependency of the test binary only (not of `anno_render_gpu`/`anno_render`), guarded by `#if defined(_WIN32)`/`#ifdef WIN32` in both the CMakeLists.txt link and the source file - wgpu's own `WGPUAdapterInfo` has no memory-size fields to read instead, and this question is explicitly about what the OS/API expose, which on this project's Windows dev host means DXGI.
- Did not touch OQ-096b's default or design a split-upload path: both are the owner's call (the packet's own "don't change the default. Prepare the options and numbers"), recorded as OQ-727 rather than acted on.

READY FOR REVIEW.
